(وَإِنْ كانَ أَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ لَظالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; (إن) is lightened from the heavy [إنّ], either inoperative or operative with its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), i.e. «وإن الشأن كان أصحاب الأيكة»; (كان) and its noun; (الأيكة) is the muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); (ظالمين) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان). (فَانْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ وَإِنَّهُما لَبِإِمامٍ مُبِينٍ): in (فانتقمنا) the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "they persisted in sin, so We took retribution"; (انتقمنا) is a verb and its agent; (منهم) is attached to (انتقمنا). In (وإنهما) the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; (إنهما) is inna and its noun, the mīm and the alif being two letters indicating the dual. There is disagreement about what they refer to: it is said the towns of the people of Lot and al-Ayka; it is said they refer to al-Ayka and Madyan, because Shuʿayb was sent to both, so when al-Ayka was mentioned, its mention pointed to Madyan and the pronoun for both was used; it is said it refers to Lot and Shuʿayb; and it is said it refers to the two accounts: the account of the destruction of Lot's people and the account of the destruction of Shuʿayb's people. The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (بإمام) is the khabar of (إنهما) — the road is called إمام because whoever travels it follows it (yaʾtammu bihi) until he reaches the place he wants; (مبين) is its naʿt (adjective). (وَلَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أَصْحابُ الْحِجْرِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ): conjoined to what preceded so that the stories run in sequence; the lām prepares for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (قد) is a particle of verification; (كذب أصحاب الحجر) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (المرسلين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). This begins the story of Ṣāliḥ. (وَآتَيْناهُمْ آياتِنا فَكانُوا عَنْها مُعْرِضِينَ): (وآتيناهم) is a verb, an agent and a first object; (آياتنا) is the second object; (فكانوا) is conjoined to (آتيناهم); kāna and its noun; (عنها) is attached to (معرضين); (معرضين) is the khabar of (كانوا). (وَكانُوا يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبالِ بُيُوتاً آمِنِينَ): (وكانوا) is conjoined; kāna and its noun; the clause (ينحتون) is its khabar; (من الجبال) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), since it was originally an adjective, or [it is attached] to (ينحتون); (بيوتا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (آمنين) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in (ينحتون), i.e. while they were secure about them from collapsing, because of the solidity and firmness of their construction, or from being targeted by raids and attacks, because they were impregnable strongholds for them. (فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّيْحَةُ مُصْبِحِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أخذتهم) is a verb and a fronted direct object; (الصيحة) is a postponed agent; (مصبحين) is a ḥāl, i.e. entering the time of morning. (فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (أغنى) is a past verb; (عنهم) is attached to (أغنى); (ما) is the fāʿil; the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause (يكسبون) is the khabar of (كانوا). It is also possible that (ما) is interrogative, a fronted object of (أغنى), and possible that (ما) is maṣdarī, with the same i'rab. (وَما خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (خلقنا السموات) is a verb, an agent and a direct object; (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (بالحق) is a ḥāl, the bāʾ being for accompaniment (mulābasa), i.e. invested with truth, wisdom and benefit. (وَإِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌ فَاصْفَحِ الصَّفْحَ الْجَمِيلَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; (آتية) is its khabar; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that implies an omitted condition); (اصفح) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, implied as "you"; (الصفح) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (الجميل) is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the words of the Exalted «وان كان أصحاب الأيكة لظالمين» there is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) whose relation is that of the occupied place [al-ḥāliyya], because al-Ayka is dense, crowded trees.
2- In His words «لبإمام مبين» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because the road is a way of arriving, and the traveller on it follows it to the end; so the thing compared-to is used in place of the thing compared.

dervis-irab:86-99.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَثانِي): what is meant by al-mathānī here is disputed. It is said to be al-Fātiḥa, because it is repeated (tuthnā) in every rakʿa, and it is seven verses; and it is said to be the seven long sūras. It is the plural of مثناة, the feminine of مثنى; it was discussed in detail in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ. The seven long sūras were called mathānī because of the repetition in them of stories, admonitions, promises and threats. The discussion of this is set out at length in the extensive works.
(عِضِينَ): the plural of عضة, whose original form is عضوة, from عضّى الشاة ("he cut the sheep into limbs"); and it is said [its original form is] عضهة, from عضهته ("I slandered him"). In al-Mukhtār: "Al-Kisāʾī said: العضة is lying and slander, and its plural is عضون, like عزة and عزون. Allah the Exalted said: «الذين جعلوا القرآن عضين». It is said that what is missing from it is the wāw, and it is from عضوته, i.e. 'I divided it', because the polytheists divided their sayings about it, calling it lies, sorcery, soothsaying and poetry. And it is said that what is missing from it is the hāʾ, its original form being عضهة, because العضة and العضين in the dialect of Quraysh mean sorcery; they call the sorcerer عاضه." Further discussion of the nouns attached to the sound masculine plural will come in the Benefits section.
(فَاصْدَعْ): so proclaim it openly and make it manifest. One says صدع بالحجة when someone speaks the argument openly, as when you say صرّح بها ("he declared it"); [it is] from الصديع, which is the dawn; and الصدع in glass is a split [al-ibāna, "separation"]. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the original sense of الصدع is splitting and separating, i.e. separate truth from falsehood. Further discussion of this wonderful expression will come in the Rhetoric section.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ الْخَلَّاقُ الْعَلِيمُ): inna, its noun and its khabar (predicate); (هو) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْناكَ سَبْعاً مِنَ الْمَثانِي وَالْقُرْآنَ الْعَظِيمَ): a resumptive statement, brought to alert the Muslims that what was sent down to them is «خبر» [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently «خير», "better"] than the goods of this world. It is said: seven caravans belonging to the Jews of Banū Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr arrived from Buṣrā and Adhriʿāt, carrying kinds of cloth, perfume, jewels and all sorts of goods. The Muslims said: "If this wealth were ours we would strengthen ourselves with it and spend it in the way of Allah." So Allah, Mighty and Exalted, said to them: "I have given you seven verses that are better than these seven caravans." The lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (آتيناك) is a past verb, its agent and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (سبعا) is the second object; (من المثاني) is a naʿt (adjective) of (سبعا); (القرآن) is conjoined to (سبعا), by way of conjoining attributes while the thing described is one; (العظيم) is an adjective of (القرآن). (لا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ): (لا) is prohibitive; (تمدن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of jussive by the prohibitive (لا); the fāʿil (agent) is latent, implied as "you"; (عينيك) is a mafʿūl bihi; (إلى ما) is attached to (تمدن); the clause (متعنا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (به) is attached to (متعنا); (أزواجا) is the object of (متعنا); (منهم) is an adjective of (أزواجا). By أزواج are meant kinds/classes among them; i.e. before the abundant blessings you have been given, all the glitter and embellishments of worldly life seem paltry. (وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَاخْفِضْ جَناحَكَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): (ولا تحزن) is conjoined to (لا تمدن); (عليهم) is attached to (تحزن); (اخفض) is also conjoined; (جناحك) is a mafʿūl bihi; (للمؤمنين) is attached to (اخفض). (وَقُلْ إِنِّي أَنَا النَّذِيرُ الْمُبِينُ): inna and its noun; (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) or a pronoun of separation; (النذير) is the khabar of (أنا) or the khabar of (إنّ); (المبين) is an adjective. (كَما أَنْزَلْنا عَلَى الْمُقْتَسِمِينَ): (كما) has two possibilities. One is that they [the kāf and mā] are attached to His words (ولقد آتيناك), i.e. We sent down to you the like of what We sent down to the People of the Book, who are «المقتسمون» (those who divided). The second is that they are attached to (النذير), i.e. there is sent down to you the like of what descended upon the People of the Book. In either case it is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (على المقتسمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنزلنا); an account of them will come. (الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا الْقُرْآنَ عِضِينَ): (الذين) is an adjective of (المقتسمين); the clause (جعلوا) is the ṣila; (القرآن) is the object of (جعلوا); (عضين) is the second object, i.e. they divided the Quran into parts, calling it sorcery, poetry and legends. There has been disagreement over these "dividers" and their stories, to an extent that would take us outside the method set for this book, so refer to it in the extensive works.
(فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَسْئَلَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ عَمَّا كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; the wāw is for the oath; (ربك) is genitive by the wāw of the oath, and both are attached to an omitted verb, implied as «أقسم» ("I swear"); the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; (لنسئلنهم) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (أجمعين) is a tawkīd (emphasis). (فَاصْدَعْ بِما تُؤْمَرُ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you know this, then proclaim"; (اصدع) is an imperative verb, its agent "you"; (بما) is attached to it; (ما) is maṣdarī or relative; (عن المشركين) is attached to (أعرض). Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī preferred that it be maṣdarī, and Ibn al-Shajarī gave the reason, saying: in it — i.e. in taking it as relative — there are five omissions. The original would be «بما تؤمر بالصدع به»; the bāʾ was omitted, giving «بالصدعه» [Translator's note: the source has «بالصدعة»]; then the al was omitted because it cannot combine with annexation, giving «بصدعه» [Translator's note: the source has «يصدعه»]; then the muḍāf (first term of the construct) was omitted, as in «واسأل القرية», giving «به»; then the preposition was omitted, as ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib said:
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded; I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
giving «تؤمره»; then the hāʾ was omitted, as it was omitted in «أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا». He only committed himself to five omissions so that it would conform to the rule for omitting a genitive resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid), because a genitive resumptive pronoun is only omitted when it is governed by the same preposition that governed the relative [noun], and when each of the two prepositions is attached to a governor like the one the other is attached to. So in Ibn al-Shajarī's words "the original is «بما تؤمر بالصدع به»", the resumptive pronoun is attached to the like of what the preposition before the relative is attached to; whereas had he said «اصدع بما تؤمر به», those conditions would not be met, because of the difference in what they are attached to: the first bāʾ is attached to «الصدع» and the second is attached to «تؤمر». (إِنَّا كَفَيْناكَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ): inna and its noun; the clause (كفيناك) is its khabar, being a verb, its agent and a direct object; (المستهزئين) is the second object. (الَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ): (الذين) is an adjective of (المستهزئين); the clause (يجعلون) is the ṣila; the wāw is the agent; (مع الله) is an adverb of place attached to something omitted that is the second object of (يجعلون); (إلها) is a mafʿūl bihi; (آخر) is an adjective; the fāʾ is resumptive; (سوف) is a particle of futurity; (يعلمون) is an imperfect verb and its agent, and the object is omitted, i.e. the outcome of their affair. (وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ بِما يَقُولُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (قد) is a particle of paucity, but here what is meant by it is frequency and verification; (نعلم) is an imperfect verb, its agent latent, implied as "We"; in (أنك), anna together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (نعلم); anna and its noun; the clause (يضيق صدرك) is its khabar; (صدرك) is the agent of (يضيق); (بما) is attached to (يضيق); the clause (يقولون) is the ṣila, and the resumptive pronoun is omitted, i.e. the sayings they say and the rumours they spread. (فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; the i'rab of (سبح بحمد ربك) was given recently; «وكن مع الساجدين» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic wording is «وَكُنْ مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ», and the analysis that follows treats it as «مع»]: kāna and its noun; (مع) is an adverb of place attached to something omitted that is its khabar; (الساجدين) is the muḍāf ilayhi. (وَاعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ): (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; (يأتيك) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after (حتى); the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; (اليقين) is the fāʿil. Death is called اليقين ("the certainty") because its occurrence is certain.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «فاصدع بما تؤمر» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). The source of the borrowing is the glass, the thing borrowed is الصدع, which is splitting, and the thing it is borrowed for is «عقوق المكلفين» [Translator's note: so in the source, lit. "the disobedience of those charged with obligations"]. It is a borrowing of the sensory for the intellectual; reference has already been made to the types of metaphor. The meaning is: declare all that has been revealed to you and make clear all that you were commanded to make clear, even if that is hard on some hearts so that they are split. The resemblance between the two lies in the effect the splitting has on hearts, the trace of which then appears on the surface of faces as contraction and expansion, and on which signs of rejection and joy show, just as [the split] appears on the surface of the cracked glass. Look at this metaphor: how marvellous it is, how far-reaching its indications and aims, and how concise, since it occurs in three words that enfold what would fill pages. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayda said: the Prophet ﷺ continued to remain hidden until this verse was revealed, and then he and his Companions came out.
It is related that a certain Bedouin, when he heard these three words, prostrated. He was asked: "Why did you prostrate?" He said: "I prostrated to the eloquence of this speech," because he grasped from it at once, without reflection, all that we have grasped after deliberation and study. From this it becomes clear to you that the Arabs were certain, from the first time they heard the Quran, that it was beyond human ability, so they did not occupy themselves with countering it, nor did their souls even suggest it to them.
2- In His words «واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين» there is an implicit metaphor; it will be discussed at length at His words «واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة».

* Benefits:
What is attached to the sound masculine plural:
Four types were assimilated to the sound masculine plural; they are declined with letters, though they are not sound masculine plurals. They are as follows:
The first: collective nouns (asmāʾ al-jumūʿ). They are: أولو in the sense of "possessors"; عالمون, a collective noun of عالَم (with a fatḥa on the lām) and not its plural, because العالم is general for rational beings and others, while العالمون is specific to rational beings, and the specific cannot be the plural of what is more general than it; and عشرون and its class, which is the rest of the decades up to ninety. All the decades occur in the Quran, and we have counted them as follows:
a- «ان يكن منكم عشرون صابرون».
b- «وواعدنا موسى ثلاثين ليلة وأتممناها بعشر فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة».
c- «فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما».
d- «فإطعام ستين مسكينا».
e- «ذرعها سبعون ذراعا».
f- «فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة».
g- «إن هذا أخي له تسع وتسعون نعجة».
The second: broken plurals in which the form of the singular is altered and which are declined with letters. They are: (بَنُونَ), plural of ابن. By analogy its sound plural would be ابنون, just as its dual is ابنان, but its sound plural differs from its dual for a morphological reason that led to the dropping of the hamza. That is, ابن is originally بنو; its final radical was dropped for lightness and replaced by the hamza of conjunction (hamzat al-waṣl). The plural returns things to their origins, so when it was pluralised the wāw returned and the hamza went; then the wāw was dropped, but what is dropped for a reason is as though present, so the hamza did not come back. As for the dual, had the wāw returned there would be nothing requiring its dropping, since it would carry a fatḥa and the fatḥa is light; it was dropped in the first place for the purpose of lightness, so if it were dropped [again] that purpose would disappear. What prevents its dropping, if it returned, and its change into alif is the sukūn of what follows it, as in بيان; and if it were dropped the word would become بنان, producing confusion with بنان of the hand (fingertips), unlike بنون — so let this be pondered. And أرضون, with a fatḥa on the rāʾ, plural of أرض with a sukūn on it; it was given this plural because it is sometimes used in a context of magnification, as in the poet's words:
لقد ضجت الأرضون إذ قام من بني ... سدوس خطيب فوق أعواد منبر
(The lands clamoured when an orator of Banū Sadūs rose upon the wooden steps of a pulpit.)
except that he gave the rāʾ a sukūn out of poetic necessity. And سنون, with a kasra on the sīn, plural of سنة with a fatḥa on it, a noun for the year; its final radical is wāw or hāʾ, because they say سنوات and سنهات. And its class, which is widespread in every three-radical noun whose final radical has been dropped and replaced by the hāʾ of the feminine and which has not been given a broken plural, such as عضة and عضين. The original of عضة is عضه with hāʾ, from العضه, which is slander and lying; in the hadith: «لا يعضه بعضكم بعضا» ("let none of you slander another"). It is said its original is عضو, from their saying عضّيته تعضية when you divided it. On the first view its final radical is hāʾ, which is indicated by its diminutive عضيهة; on the second it is wāw, which is indicated by its plural عضوات; both the diminutive and the plural return things to their origins. And عزة and عزين: العزة, with a kasra on the ʿayn and a fatḥa on the zāy, is originally عزى, so its final radical is yāʾ; it is a group of people, and العزين are the various groups, because each group traces its lineage (taʿtazī) to other than whom the other traces its lineage. And ثبة and ثبين: الثبة, with a ḍamma on the thāʾ and a fatḥa on the bāʾ, is a company; its original is ثبو, and it is said ثبي from ثبّيت, i.e. "I gathered", so its final radical is wāw on the first view and yāʾ on the second. This is not permitted in the like of اسم, أخت and بنت, because the substitute in them for their dropped final radical is other than the hāʾ. As for اسم, its original is سمو; its final radical was dropped and replaced by the hamza at its beginning. As for أخت and بنت, their originals are أخو and بنو; their final radical was dropped and replaced by the tāʾ of the feminine, not the hāʾ of the feminine. The difference between them is that the tāʾ of the feminine in these two is not changed to hāʾ in pause and is written open, whereas the hāʾ of the feminine is paused on with hāʾ and written tied (marbūṭa). Nor [is it permitted] in the like of شاة and شفة, because they were given the broken plurals شفاه and شياه. Al-Jawharī said: they were not given plurals with letters only because the Arabs made do with their broken plurals instead of their sound plurals.
The third of what is assimilated to this plural: sound plurals that do not fulfil the conditions of the plural, such as أهلون and وابلون, because أهل and وابل are neither proper names nor adjectives, and because وابل is not rational; and it is well known that the condition of this plural is that it be for the proper name of a rational being or its adjective.
The fourth: what is used as a name from this plural and from what is attached to it. The first is like زيدون used as the name of a person; the second is like عليون, which is attached to this plural and is used as the name of the highest part of Paradise. The Exalted said: «إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين وما أدراك ما عليون». There are other details that need not be set down, because they are below the level of the eloquent; for this reason we have refrained from mentioning them, and they may be consulted in the extensive works.

dervis-irab:26-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصلصال): dry clay that rings when struck, while it is unbaked; once baked it is pottery (fakhkhār). They said: if you imagine in its sound a prolongation, it is ṣalīl; if you imagine in it a repetition, it is ṣalṣala. It was also said that it is a doubling of ṣalla "to stink"; and it was said: al-ṣalṣāl is dry clay which, when tapped, gives off a sound, that is, a ringing (ṣalṣala); it has the sense of al-muṣalṣal, like al-zilzāl in the sense of al-muzalzal, and the pattern faʿlāl can also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), such as al-zilzāl. Concerning the pattern (wazn) of this kind, that is, a word whose first and second radicals are repeated, there is a disagreement. It was said that its pattern is faʿfaʿ, the fāʾ and the ʿayn being repeated, with no lām in the word; this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and it is a mistake, because the minimum of roots is three: fāʾ, ʿayn and lām. Al-Farrāʾ in fact departed from it and said that its pattern is faʿfal. It was also said that its origin is faʿʿal with doubled ʿayn, its origin being ṣallal; when three identical letters came together, the second was replaced by a letter of the same kind as the first radical of the word. Some restricted this disagreement to cases where the meaning is not impaired by dropping the third letter, such as lamlam and kabkab, for you say of them lamma and kabba; but if the meaning is not sound with its dropping, as in simsim, there is no disagreement about the originality of all the letters. It was also said that its pattern is faʿlal with repetition of the lām, the first of the two being converted into a letter of the same kind as the first radical of the word. In al-Qāmūs: al-ṣalṣāl is dry clay which rings of itself, that is, makes a sound; and one says ṣalṣala ṣalṣalatan of jewellery or a bridle, meaning it made a sound; of thunder, its sound was clear; of a bell, its sound resounded; and ṣalṣala fulānan means he threatened so-and-so. Furthermore, an augment has occurred as a fourth letter after the first lām in a good number of nouns, amounting to nearly ten patterns, among them:
faʿlīl, which occurs in nouns and adjectives. The noun is e.g. qindīl and burṭīl; the adjective e.g. shunẓīr and hamhīm. The qindīl is well known; the burṭīl is a long stone about a cubit in length; the shunẓīr is the ill-natured person; the hamhīm is the one who repeats and mutters, and one says "a hamhīm donkey", that is, one with repetition in its voice, from al-hamhama.
Among them also faʿlūl, in nouns and adjectives. The noun is e.g. ʿuṣfūr and zunbūr; the adjective e.g. sirḥūb and qirḍūb. The ʿuṣfūr (sparrow) and the zunbūr (wasp) are well known; the sirḥūb is the tall one; the qirḍūb is the poor man, and it is also one of the names of the sword, and sometimes a thief is called qirḍūb.
Among them also faʿlīl with ḍamma on the fāʾ, sukūn on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the first lām. They said, as an adjective: ghurniq, which is the lofty master; the ghurniq is also a long-necked water bird. Al-Jawharī said: when men are described by it, one says ghirniq with kasra on the ghayn and ghurniq with ḍamma, and the plural is gharāniq with fatḥa, and gharānīq.
Among them also faʿlūl, which occurs in nouns and adjectives. The noun is e.g. firdaws and ḥirdhawn; the adjective ʿalṭūs. The firdaws is the garden; the ḥirdhawn is a small creature like the sandgrouse (qaṭāh); the ʿalṭūs is the sturdy she-camel.
Among them also faʿlūl in nouns and adjectives. The noun is e.g. qarbūs and zarjūn; the adjective qarqūs and ḥalkūk. The qarbūs is the well-known pommel of the saddle; the zarjūn is wine, so called because of its colour, its origin in Persian being zarkūn (zar being gold and kūn colour); Abū ʿAmr al-Jarmī said: it is a red dye.
Among them also faʿlūl with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn, sukūn on the lām and fatḥa on the lām. They said kanhawr and balhawr. The kanhawr is the great cloud; the balhawr is one of the kings of India — every great king of theirs is called balhawr — and we do not know it as a proper noun.
Among them also faʿlāl, which occurs only in reduplicated four-radical words, as a noun or an adjective. The noun is e.g. al-zilzāl and al-ḥathḥāth; the adjective e.g. al-ṣalṣāl and al-qasqās. The zilzāl is a maṣdar like al-zilzala; the ḥathḥāth has the sense of al-ḥathḥatha; the ṣalṣāl is pure clay mixed with sand, which rings when it dries, and if it is baked it is pottery; the qasqās is the guide who leads the way. One word has come on faʿlāl that is not reduplicated: they said nāqa bihā khazʿāl, a she-camel with an ugly gait from a disease.
Among them also faʿlāl with kasra on the fāʾ, which occurs as a noun and an adjective. The noun is e.g. sirbāl and ḥimlāq; the adjective sirdāḥ and hilbāj. The sirbāl is the shirt; the ḥimlāq is the part of the eye covered by the eyelids; the sirdāḥ is the wide land; the hilbāj is the one with many faults.
Among them also faʿallal with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn and doubling of the first lām, which occurs as a noun and an adjective. The noun is e.g. shafalḥ and hamarrajа; the adjective al-ʿadabbas and al-ʿamallas. The shafalḥ is a certain fruit, and it may be an adjective meaning thick-lipped; the hamarraja is mixing — one says hamrajtu ʿalayhi al-khabar, "I muddled the report for him"; the ʿadabbas is the huge one; the ʿamallas is the light one, and the wolf is also called ʿamallas. Al-Shanfarā said:
ولي دونكم أهلون سيد عملّس ... وأرقط زهلول وعرفاء جيأل
(I have, besides you, other kinsfolk: a wolf, swift and lean; a spotted, smooth-coated leopard; and a long-maned hyena.)
Among them also fuʿallal with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the ʿayn, which is rare. They said al-ṣufarraq and al-zumarrudh; both are nouns: the ṣufarraq is a plant, and the zumarrudh is the well-known gem (emerald).
(حَمَإٍ): al-ḥamaʾ is black mud whose smell has changed from lying a long time; it is also called al-ḥamaʾa.
(مَسْنُونٍ): foul-smelling, from sanantu al-ḥajara ʿalā al-ḥajar, "I rubbed the stone against the stone", for what flows between them is foul-smelling and is called sanīn. It was also said: poured out, emptied, that is, a human form was emptied out, just as forms are poured from molten metals into their moulds. The verb sanna is distinguished by the abundance of its meanings, to the point that one almost becomes bewildered: one says sanna yasinnu al-sikkīn (of the root naṣara type), meaning he sharpened and whetted it; one says "this is of what sannaka on food", that is, whets you for eating it and gives you an appetite for it; sanna al-rumḥ, he fitted the spearhead to it; sanna al-asnān, he cleaned the teeth with a tooth-stick; sanna al-ʿuqda, he untied the knot; sanna al-ibil, he drove the camels quickly; sanna al-rajul, he stabbed him with a spearhead, bit him with his teeth, broke his teeth, praised him and extolled him; sanna al-amr, he made the matter clear, easy and current; sanna al-ṭarīqa, he travelled along the way; sanna ʿalayhim al-sunna, he laid down the sunna for them; sanna al-ṭīn, he worked clay into pottery; sanna al-shayʾ, he shaped it; sanna al-māʾ aw al-turāb, he poured water or earth gently; sannat al-ʿayn al-damʿ, the eye poured out tears; sanna al-amīr raʿiyyatahu, the ruler governed his subjects well. One says: "so-and-so initiated (sanna) a path of good", that is, he began a matter of righteousness unknown to his people. This is among the wonders of our noble language.
(الْجَانَّ): it is to the jinn what Adam is to mankind.
(السَّمُومِ): the fire of intense heat that penetrates the pores; it was also said to be a fire without smoke that penetrates the pores; and it was said: al-samūm is whatever kills through excessive heat, whether from sun, wind or fire, because it enters the pores, which are the holes, and kills; its plural is samāʾim.
(رَجِيمٌ): driven away. In al-Miṣbāḥ: al-rajam, with fatḥa on both letters, is stones, and al-rajm is the grave, so called because of the stones that gather over it; and rajamtuhu rajman (like qatala) means I struck him with stones. In al-Qāmūs: "al-rajm: cursing, reviling, expelling and abandoning"; the marjūm is the one driven away and cursed, and "Allah cursed him" means He drove him away and distanced him. Al-Shammākh said:
وماء قد وردت لوصل أروى ... عليه الطير كالورق اللّجين
ذعرت به القطا ونفيت عنه ... مقام الذئب كالرجل اللعين
(Many a water have I come to, to be united with Arwā, with birds upon it like silver coins; I startled the sandgrouse there and drove from it the wolf's lair, like a cursed man.)

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ صَلْصالٍ مِنْ حَمَإٍ مَسْنُونٍ) The wāw is resumptive (istināfiyya); the lām is the apodosis of an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty (taḥqīq); خلقنا الإنسان is a verb, agent and direct object; من صلصال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلقنا; and من حمأ may be an adjective of صلصال, and may be a substitute (badal) for the phrase من صلصال with repetition of the preposition; and مسنون is an adjective of حمأ.
(وَالْجَانَّ خَلَقْناهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ مِنْ نارِ السَّمُومِ) والجان is accusative by iḥtighāl (pre-occupation of the verb with a pronoun); خلقناه is a verb, agent and direct object; من قبل is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and من نار السموم is attached to خلقناه. (وَإِذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ إِنِّي خالِقٌ بَشَراً مِنْ صَلْصالٍ مِنْ حَمَإٍ مَسْنُونٍ) The adverb is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; the clause قال ربك is annexed to the adverb; للملائكة is attached to قال; إن and its noun; خالق is its predicate; بشرا is a direct object of خالق; and من صلصال من حمأ مسنون has been parsed above. (فَإِذا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِي فَقَعُوا لَهُ ساجِدِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of the condition; the clause سويته is annexed to the adverb; نفخت is conjoined to سويته; فيه is attached to نفخت; and من روحي is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "a spirit from My spirit", the meaning being the giving of life, there being in truth no blowing and nothing blown; فقعوا: the fāʾ is the connector of the apodosis of إذا; وقعوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the agent; له is attached to ساجدين; and ساجدين is a ḥāl. (فَسَجَدَ الْمَلائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted clause, i.e. "so He created him, fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, so the angels prostrated"; and كلهم and أجمعون are two emphases (tawkīd), for further establishing the meaning and fixing it in the mind. Al-Mubarrad was asked about this verse and said: "Had He said 'the angels prostrated', it would be possible that only some of them prostrated; when He said 'all of them', this possibility disappeared and it became clear that they prostrated in their entirety; and then after this a possibility remained, namely whether they prostrated all at once or each one at a different time; so when He said 'all together', it became clear that they all prostrated at once." (إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبى أَنْ يَكُونَ مَعَ السَّاجِدِينَ) The discussion of this exception has gone before: that it is a connected exception (muttaṣil), either because he was a jinni submerged among thousands of angels and so was counted among them by predominance, or because he was truly one of them; and it is possible that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), in which case what follows attaches to it, i.e. "but Iblīs refused to be with them". أبى is a past verb; أن يكون is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative as the direct object of أبى; the noun of يكون is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", i.e. Iblīs; مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted predicate of يكون; and الساجدين is a genitive annexed term (muḍāf ilayhi). (قالَ: يا إِبْلِيسُ ما لَكَ أَلَّا تَكُونَ مَعَ السَّاجِدِينَ) يا is a particle of vocative; إبليس is a vocative, a single proper noun; ما is an interrogative noun of rebuke, a mubtadaʾ; ولك is its khabar; and أن and what is in its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "what is the matter with you, not being with the prostrators?"; and أن لا تكون مع الساجدين has been parsed above. (قالَ: لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأَسْجُدَ لِبَشَرٍ خَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ صَلْصالٍ مِنْ حَمَإٍ مَسْنُونٍ) لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; أكن is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), which is for emphasising the negation; أسجد is an imperfect verb made accusative by an obligatorily implied أن after it, and the preposition and its genitive noun are the predicate of أكن; ولبشر is attached to أسجد; the clause خلقته is an adjective of بشر; and من صلصال من حمأ مسنون has been parsed above. (قالَ فَاخْرُجْ مِنْها فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa) because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you persist and disobey, then go out"; منها is attached to اخرج; the fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya); إن with its noun and predicate; and the clause has no grammatical position. (وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ اللَّعْنَةَ إِلى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; عليك is the fronted predicate of إن; اللعنة is its postponed noun; and إلى يوم الدين is a ḥāl, i.e. "abiding until that limit". (قالَ رَبِّ فَأَنْظِرْنِي إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ) رب is a vocative from which the particle of vocative has been omitted, annexed to the first-person yāʾ; the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ because it occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if You have decreed this recompense against me, then grant me respite", that is, give me time; إلى يوم is attached to أنظرني; يبعثون is an imperfect passive verb and the wāw is the deputy agent; and the clause يبعثون is annexed to it. He asked for respite only until the day on which they are resurrected so as to find room and latitude for leading astray, and deliverance at death, since there is no death after the time of resurrection; so He answered him as to the first and not the second, that is, "be given respite until the last of the days of obligation (taklīf)", as will come. (قالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إن with its noun; and من المنظرين is its predicate. (إِلى يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ الْمَعْلُومِ) إلى يوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to المنظرين; الوقت is a genitive annexed term; and المعلوم is an adjective. (قالَ رَبِّ بِما أَغْوَيْتَنِي لَأُزَيِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) رب is a vocative as above; and بما: the bāʾ is the bāʾ of oath and ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. "I swear by Your leading me astray", and the clause لأزينن is the answer to the oath, whose like has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf; and it was said that the bāʾ is causal; both are permissible. لأزينن: the lām is the answer to the oath, or it is the lām that prepares for an oath if the bāʾ is causal; and أزينن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa; ولهم is attached
to أزينن; في الأرض is a ḥāl; ولأغوينهم is conjoined to لأزينن; and أجمعين is an emphasis of the pronoun. (إِلَّا عِبادَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ) إلا is a particle of exception; عبادك is the excepted; المخلصين is an adjective; and منهم is a ḥāl. (قالَ هذا صِراطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) هذا is a mubtadaʾ; صراط is a khabar; علي is attached to an omitted adjective, i.e. "a right"; and مستقيم is a second adjective, i.e. "this is a path of truth that I am bound to observe and not transgress, and it is:" (إِنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ) the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) of the straight path which I have made obligatory upon Myself to adhere to; إن and its noun; the clause ليس is the predicate; لك is the fronted predicate of ليس; عليهم is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of سلطان; and سلطان is the postponed noun of ليس.
Ibn Hishām said: "The saying of many grammarians regarding His words, the Exalted: ﴿إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك﴾ is that it is evidence for the permissibility of excepting the greater from the lesser. The correct view is that what is meant by 'servants' is the sincere ones (al-mukhlaṣūn), not all those owned, and that the exception is disconnected, by the evidence of its absence in verse 65 of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: ﴿إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان وكفى بربك وكيلا﴾." Al-Damāmīnī followed him up, saying: "His preference for the exception being disconnected is open to objection, since it is a departure from the default without necessity, for it is possible to take the exception as connected, which is the default, and for 'servants' to mean all those owned; and it does no harm that the verse of al-Isrāʾ is without an exception, because there 'servants' is meant to be the sincere ones, so the exception was left out. It may be answered that the Qurʾān explains itself in parts: when a word is repeated in it and it has one possible meaning in one place, and in another that meaning and others, the latter is taken in that meaning and no other. And the disconnected exception, though contrary to the default, is nonetheless eloquent and common."
(إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْغاوِينَ) It was said it is an exception from other than the genus, because what is meant by "My servants" is the monotheists, and the follower of Satan is not a monotheist; and it was said it is from the genus, because "My servants" are all those under obligation; and من الغاوين is a ḥāl. (وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمَوْعِدُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); موعدهم is the khabar of إن; and أجمعين is an emphasis of the pronoun. (لَها سَبْعَةُ أَبْوابٍ لِكُلِّ بابٍ مِنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَقْسُومٌ) لها is a fronted predicate; سبعة أبواب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ولكل باب is a fronted predicate; منهم is a ḥāl because it was an adjective of جزء; جزء is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and مقسوم is also an adjective of جزء. What is meant by "portion" is a group.

* Rhetoric:
1- Conciseness (ījāz) in His words «قال هذا صراط علي مستقيم»; perhaps it is among the most eloquent of concisions, because it is the counterpart of conciseness by omission; it is conciseness by implication (ījāz bi-l-taqdīr), and it is of two kinds: the first, that whose wording equals its meaning; the second, that whose meaning exceeds its wording, and it is called qaṣr, since its wording indicates many possibilities and many implications, and it cannot be expressed by words like its own or of its number; indeed that is impossible. For His word «هذا» is a pointing that indicates nearness, as if He were pointing to what is before their eyes, within their hearing and within reach of their hands; and «صراط» indicates the trodden road that leads its traveller to whatever destination he chooses for himself; but a road may be crooked, twisting, with many turns, so that the traveller is lost in its wildernesses and the signs of guidance are confused for him in travelling it; so He brought the word «مستقيم», and the straight line is the shortest distance between two points, and the least deviation takes it out of the norms and bounds of straightness; and the word «علي» means obligation and necessity, as you say "I swear by Allah's covenant that I will do such and such", and so you convey that you have bound yourself to what is a right whose fulfilment is owed. Then the pointing contained everything that the exception afterwards includes, namely His words «إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين», as if He took upon Himself and made binding upon His own Self a right from which there is no release, namely the deliverance of the sincere ones from his misleading. The definiteness of «المخلصين» also contains what confirms this meaning and fixes it in the mind, for the definiteness in it, along with affirming the attribute for the one described, namely sincerity, is a magnification of their status, a declaration of their rank, and of the cutting off of the claws of misleading from them, and the blunting of the picks of criticism being directed at them. This verse is few words, yet it contains these purposes. We must present examples from outside the Qurʾān, not because they rise to its level but because they revolve in its orbit, hover around it and draw from its sources. Listen to this wondrous story:
When al-Muhallab ibn Abī Ṣufra sent Abū al-Ḥasan al-Madāʾinī to al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf to inform him of the news of the Azāriqa, he spoke to him a concise speech like the one we are concerned with here. Al-Ḥajjāj asked him, saying: "How did you leave al-Muhallab?" He said: "He has attained what he hoped for and is safe from what he feared." He said: "How is he with his troops?" He said: "A compassionate father." He said: "How are his troops with him?" He said: "Dutiful sons." He said: "How is their contentment with him?" He said: "He has been generous to them with his bounty and enriched them with his justice." He said: "What do you do when you meet the enemy?" He said: "We meet them with our fortune and they meet us with theirs." He said: "So it is when fortune meets fortune." He said: "Tell me about the sons of al-Muhallab." He said: "They are the saddle-blankets of battle by night, the guardians of the saddles by day." He said: "Which of them is best?" He said: "They are like a closed ring, whose two ends are not known." Al-Ḥajjāj said to his companions: "By Allah, this is the decisive speech that is not artificial." Consider al-Ḥajjāj's description of the speech: he described the concise, eloquent speech with what approaches it in conciseness and eloquence; and no wonder, for al-Ḥajjāj was a sign in mastery of the language and knowledge of its properties. Al-Zajjāj related in his Amālī, saying: "Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Durayd informed us, saying: Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī informed us, from al-Aṣmaʿī, who said: Four men never made a grammatical error, in earnest or in jest:
al-Shaʿbī, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf and Ibn al-Qarriyya, and al-Ḥajjāj was the most eloquent of them. One day he said to his cook: 'Cook for us makhalla and put plenty of al-fījan on it' (that is, rue, a plant whose leaf is like thyme) 'and make for us mazʿaz.' The cook did not understand him, so he asked one of his companions, who said to him: 'Cook him sikbāj, put plenty of rue in it, and make him fālūdhaj salis.'" You will see examples of conciseness in many places, by which the condition of the book will be fulfilled.
2- The exception in His words, the Exalted: «فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون إلا إبليس». Had this exception not been preceded by this precaution (iḥtirās) in His words كلهم أجمعون, it would have been possible, as we indicated in the i'rab, that among the angels there were some who did not prostrate, so that Iblīs would have a precedent and not be alone in this grave sin, since the definite article might be for a specific referent (ʿahd) and not for the genus. Since this difficulty would arise in the speech if it were limited to less than emphasis, emphasis had to be brought, so that it would be known that the definite article is for the genus, and the difficulty is removed by this precaution; at that point the sin of Iblīs becomes grave, since he separated himself from the whole of the Highest Assembly and broke the consensus of the angels, so he deserves to be singled out for this curse until the end of time. Furthermore, the exception that the rhetoricians speak of is other than the exception known to the grammarians; so it is of two kinds, linguistic and technical. As for the linguistic, the grammarians have finished establishing it; as for the technical, it is the one we are concerned with, and it belongs to the science of bayān (figurative expression), and splendid examples of it will come in this wondrous book.

dervis-irab:1-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ وَقُرْآنٍ مُبِينٍ) The parsing of الر has already preceded; تلك is a mubtadaʾ; آيات الكتاب is the khabar; قرآن is conjoined to الكتاب; and مبين is an adjective of القرآن. It is permissible to conjoin قرآن to الكتاب even though what is meant is one thing, because of the verbal plurality and difference in it, and for the additional attribute in the conjoined word, namely مبين. Beautiful is the saying of al-Bayḍāwī:
"The indefiniteness of al-Qurʾān is for magnification, and likewise the definiteness of al-Kitāb."
(رُبَما يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ كانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ) ربما: kāffa and makfūfa. Abū Ḥayyān said: "Since rubba, according to most, does not enter upon a future verb, they interpreted يود as meaning wadda, because the future in Allah's reports is like the past owing to the certainty of its occurrence, so it is as if it were said 'they wished'. That is not necessary; rather it may enter upon the future, though rarely in comparison with its entering upon the past. Among the instances in which it occurs with the future is the saying of Hind, mother of Muʿāwiya:
يا رب قائلة غدا ... يا لهف أم معاويه
(O how many a woman will say tomorrow: Alas for Muʿāwiya's mother!)
and the saying of Jaḥdar:
فإن أهلك فرب فتى سيبكي ... عليّ مهذّب رخص البنان
(If I perish, many a refined, soft-fingered youth will weep for me.)
A lengthy discussion of it will come in the chapter on benefits." يود الذين: an imperfect verb and agent; the clause كفروا is a ṣila; لو is maṣdariyya (introducing a verbal noun) because it occurs after يود, and with what follows it is in the interpretation of a maṣdar which is the object of the wishing, the meaning being "they wish their being Muslims". It is also possible that لو is the conditional of impossibility (imtināʿiyya), its apodosis omitted, its implied form being "had they been Muslims they would have been glad of that, since they would have been delivered from what they are in", and on this assumption the object of يود is "salvation", that is: "often would those who disbelieved wish for salvation." (ذَرْهُمْ يَأْكُلُوا وَيَتَمَتَّعُوا وَيُلْهِهِمُ الْأَمَلُ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ) ذرهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object. It has already been mentioned that this imperative, and the imperative دع, are not used in the past tense except rarely; rather their imperfect is used, as in «ونذرهم في طغيانهم». يأكلوا is jussive as the answer to the imperative; ويتمتعوا is conjoined to يأكلوا, and likewise يلههم الأمل, with الأمل as the fāʿil. فسوف: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (eloquent fāʾ); سوف is a particle of the future; يعلمون is a verb and agent, and the object is omitted, that is, "the outcome of their affair and the evil of their doing".
(وَما أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا وَلَها كِتابٌ مَعْلُومٌ) The wāw is resumptive; ما is negative; أهلكنا is a verb and agent; من is a redundant preposition; قرية is genitive in form and accusative in position as direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; the wāw is circumstantial; ولها is a preposed khabar; كتاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; معلوم is an adjective of كتاب; and the clause is circumstantial. It is also said that the wāw is redundant. Al-Zamakhsharī preferred another aspect, namely that the clause لها كتاب معلوم is an adjective of قرية. He said: "The norm is that the wāw does not intervene between them, as in His saying «وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا لها منذرون»; it intervened only to confirm the attachment of the attribute to the thing described, as one says of the ḥāl: 'Zayd came to me with a garment on him' and 'and with a garment on him'." More discussion of this construction will come in the chapter on benefits.
(ما تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَها وَما يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ) ما is negative; تسبق is an imperfect verb; من is a redundant preposition; أمة is the fāʿil of تسبق in position, though genitive in form; أجلها is a direct object; وما يستأخرون is conjoined to ما تسبق. The words أجلها were construed according to the form of أمة, so they are singular and feminine, and His words وما يستأخرون according to its meaning, so they are plural and masculine. (وَقالُوا: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِي نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ إِنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ) The wāw is resumptive; قالوا is a verb and agent; the clause «يا أيها الذي نزل» etc. is the quoted speech; يا is a particle of address; أي is an indefinite specific vocative (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative; the hāʾ is for attention; الذي is a badal (substitute) for أي; the clause نزل is a ṣila; عليه is attached to نزل; الذكر is a nāʾib fāʿil; إن with its ism; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and مجنون is the khabar of إن. (لَوْ ما تَأْتِينا بِالْمَلائِكَةِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) لو ما is a particle of exhortation (taḥḍīḍ) like hallā, and it can also be a particle of "prevention due to existence" (imtināʿ li-wujūd). The difference between them is that the exhortative one is followed only by a verb, overt or implied, while the one of prevention is followed only by nouns. This has already been explained at length, and further discussion of لو ما will come. تأتينا is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; بالملائكة is attached to تأتينا; إن is conditional; كنت is كان with its ism; من الصادقين is its khabar; and the apodosis of إن is omitted, its implied form being "you would have brought us the angels".
(ما نُنَزِّلُ الْمَلائِكَةَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَما كانُوا إِذاً مُنْظَرِينَ) A resumptive speech brought as a rebuttal of their claim; it contains a scrambled laff wa-nashr (jumbled enfolding and unfolding), whose ruling will come in the chapter on rhetoric. ما is negative; ننزل is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "we"; الملائكة is the direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; بالحق is a ḥāl, that is, "accompanied by the truth", so the bāʾ is for accompaniment; it may be attached to ننزل, and al-Zamakhsharī made it an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "only a descent accompanied by the truth"; all are permissible. The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كانوا is كان with its ism; إذن is a particle of response and consequence that is not operative; and منظرين is the khabar of كان. (إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ) إن with its ism; نحن is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the ism of إن, or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; the clause نزلنا is the khabar of إن; وإنا is conjoined; له is attached to حافظون; the lām is the shifted lām; and حافظون is the khabar of إنا. (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فِي شِيَعِ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; من قبلك is an adjective of the omitted direct object understood from the expression of sending, that is, "messengers before you"; and في شيع الأولين is another adjective of the omitted object. al-Shiyaʿ is the plural of shīʿa, which is a group agreeing upon a way and doctrine. (وَما يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; يأتيهم is a verb and direct object; من is a redundant preposition; رسول is genitive in form and nominative in position as fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction; كانوا is كان with its ism; به is attached to يستهزئون; the clause يستهزئون is the khabar of كانوا; and the clause كانوا به يستهزئون is a ḥāl or an adjective of رسول.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "وما يأتيهم is the narration of a past state, because ما does not enter upon an imperfect unless it is in the position of ḥāl, nor upon a past unless it is close to the present." What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is the view of most: that ما restricts the imperfect to the present and specifies it for it. Others held that ما often enters upon the imperfect intending the present, and also enters upon it intending the future, and in support they recited the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
أودى بنيّ وأعقبوني حسرة ... عند الرقاد وعبرة ما تقلع
(My sons perished and left me grief at the time of sleep, and a tear that does not cease.)
and the saying of al-Aʿshā, praising the Messenger, peace be upon him:
له نافلات ما يغب نوالها ... وليس عطاء اليوم مانعه غدا
(He has gifts whose bestowal never lapses, and today's giving does not prevent his giving tomorrow.)

* Rhetoric:
1- Expression by the opposite: in His saying «ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين». The scholars of rhetoric differed over what is meant by this expression. The grammarians have established that rubbamā enters only upon the past; so what is meant by the sense of reduction (taqlīl) that rubba gives? The first was answered by saying that what is awaited in Allah's reports is like the past that is certain in its realisation, so it is as if it were said "often did they wish". The second was answered by saying that this is a way found in the manner of the Arabs in their saying "perhaps you will regret what you did" and "often does a man regret what he does", and they have no doubt of his regret and do not intend to make it little; the wise guard against exposing themselves to what is merely supposed just as they guard against what is certain and established. This answer is beautiful, but more beautiful than it is to say that the Arabs express a meaning in a way that conveys the opposite of what they intend, among which is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
ولجدت حتى كدت تبخل حائلا ... للمنتهى ومن السرور بكاء
(You were so generous that you almost seemed stingy, barred from the utmost; and from joy there is weeping.)
Reference has already been made to this beautiful art, and both of these aspects take the speech as exaggeration with a kind of awakening to it, the reliance in that being on the context of the speech.
2- The scrambled laff wa-nashr: this art was mentioned before, namely in His saying the Exalted: ما ننزل ... in reply to their second statement, which is «لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة». As for His reply to their first statement, which is «إنك لمجنون», it is His saying: «إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون»; then He followed that with His saying «ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك» to the end of the verse, meaning that this is their habit and the habit of the Jāhiliyya with all the prophets; so do not grieve, and follow those before you and take them as your example.

* Benefits:
1- (رب): It is also said rubbat, rubbamā and rubbatamā, and it is sometimes lightened (rubba). It is a preposition of reduction or of multiplication, as is understood from the context, and it enters only upon an indefinite noun; it is in the ruling of a redundant particle, so it is not attached to anything, as in "rubba jahlin rufiʿa" (many an ignorance has been raised). When mā is attached to it, mā prevents it from operating, so it may enter upon verbs and definite nouns, and you say rubbamā aqbala al-Khalīl and rubbamā al-Khalīl muqbil. It sometimes remains operative, as in "rubbamā ḍarbatin bi-sayfin ṣaqīl" (many a stroke with a polished sword), and it is prevented by mā, in which case it enters upon the noun and the verb and becomes like a particle of commencement, followed by a sentence made of a verb and agent, as in the verse:
ربما تجزع النفوس من الأمر له فرجة كحل العقال
(Often do souls grow anxious at a matter that has an opening like the loosing of a hobble.)
and by a mubtadaʾ and khabar, as in the verse of Abū Dūʾād al-Iyādī:
ربما الجامل المؤبل فيهم ... وعناجيج بينهنّ المهار
(Often among them are the herd of camels and thoroughbred horses with foals among them.)
The wāw may take its place, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وليل كموج البحر أرخى سدوله ... عليّ بأنواع الهموم ليبتلي
(And many a night, like the waves of the sea, let down its curtains upon me with all kinds of cares to test me.)
as the fāʾ also takes its place, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays again:
فمثلك حبلى قد طرقت ومرضع ... فألهيتها عن ذي تمائم محول
(Many a woman like you, pregnant and nursing, have I visited by night, and distracted her from her amulet-wearing child of a year.)
Now, rubba in the verse means multiplication, as the poet said:
رب رفد هرقته ذلك اليوم ... وأسرى من معشر أقيال
(Many a gift did I pour out that day, and many captives from a company of chieftains.)
As for the reason it enters upon an indefinite noun and is specific to it: because the indefinite denotes generality, so reduction is permissible in it for its admitting reduction, and multiplication for its admitting multiplication; while the definite is a known quantity and admits neither reduction nor multiplication. However, in latitude it may enter upon the pronoun as it enters upon the overt noun, like the entry of the kāf in poetic necessity, as in the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:
كل الذنابات شمالا كثبا ... وأم أوعال كها أو أقربا
(All the Dhunābāt are to the left, close by, and Umm Awʿāl is like it, or nearer.)
Except that the pronoun after rubba is obligatorily singular and masculine, and is explained by a tamyīz (specification) that follows it, as in "rubbahu rajulan ʿaraftuhu" (many a man I have known) and "rubbahu imraʾatan laqiyahā" (many a woman he has met). Ibn al-Naḥḥās said:
"There is disagreement about the pronoun returning to an indefinite noun, whether it is definite or indefinite. If we say that the pronoun of an indefinite noun is indefinite, as al-Sīrāfī, al-Zamakhsharī and a group held, there is no problem in rubba's entering upon the pronoun, because, being vague from the aspect of its coming before the explicand and from the aspect of its being used for the singular, dual and plural in one form, and general from the aspect of its being explained by an indefinite, it has acquired such vagueness and generality that it approaches the indefinite, so rubba may enter upon it. Shaykh Ibn al-Naḥḥās said: the word governed in the genitive by it, or by what stands in its place, must have an attribute first. Some of them said that this is not necessary, and some said it is necessary, such as Abū ʿAlī al-Zamakhsharī [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably Abū ʿAlī al-Shalawbīn is meant, or the name is a scribal error] and Ibn ʿUṣfūr, arguing that the attribute in an indefinite noun is for specification, so it gives the thing described a reduction, and this agrees with the intended meaning that rubba is for reduction." Shaykh Bahāʾ al-Dīn also said: "It is permissible to say 'rubba rajulin wa-akhīhi' but not 'rubba akhīhi', because in second positions what is not permitted in first positions is permitted, since, when it is second, what precedes it has already given the position its due in what it requires, so latitude in the second matter is permissible, unlike when we bring latitude in the first matter, for then we give the position nothing of what it deserves. This is if we do not say that what is annexed to the pronoun of an indefinite is indefinite; if we say it is indefinite, the permissibility is all the more allowable." He said: "The governing word of it must have the sense of the past, as in your saying 'rubba rajulin jawādin laqītuhu' (many a generous man I met), or 'anā lāqin' or 'huwa mulqan'; and you do not say 'rubba rajulin jawādin sa-alqā' or 'la-alqayanna', because reduction is common in the past, but not so in the future, since it is not known so that its reduction could be established." He said: it always requires the first place in the sentence for its resemblance to the particle of negation, because reduction is close to negation: negation is the nullification of a thing, and its reduction is a nearness to its nullification, and because the Arabs used the little in the place of negation. The poet said:
قلما يبرح المطيع هواه ... كلفا ذا صبابة وجنون
(Seldom does the obedient one cease to follow his passion, smitten, full of ardour and madness.)
Its meaning: "the obedient one does not cease to follow his passion smitten."
There are discussions relating to rubba that the scope of these benefits does not allow.
2- The wāw of ḥāl also: among the things in which the grammarians fell into an illusion is their stipulation that the wāw of ḥāl must not be joined to the affirmative illā. It is strange that Ibn Hishām fell into this illusion in his commentary on the Alfiyya of Ibn Mālik, and Shaykh Khālid al-Azharī followed him in his illusion, for this is attested in eloquent speech, namely in this verse «وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا ولها كتاب معلوم» and in the saying of the poet, as the commentator on al-Lubb said:
نعم امرأ هرم لم تعر نائبه ... إلا وكان لمرتاع بها وزرا
(What an excellent man Harim is: no calamity of his has befallen but that he was a refuge for the terrified in it.)
It is as if al-Zamakhsharī followed those who said it is not permissible, so he made the clause an adjective and the wāw for confirming the attachment of the attribute to the thing described.
3- لو ما: law mā and lawlā have two aspects. The first is that they indicate the prevention of their apodosis because of the existence of what follows them, so they are specific to nominal sentences, and to this Ibn Mālik pointed in his saying in al-Khulāṣa:
لولا ولو ما يلزمان الابتداء ... إذا امتناعا بوجود عقدا
(Lawlā and law mā require the mubtadaʾ when they are tied to prevention by existence.)
as in His saying the Exalted «لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين» and the saying of the poet:
لو ما الاصاخة للوشاة لكان لي ... من بعد سخطك في رضاك رجاء
(Were it not for listening to the slanderers, I would have hope, after your anger, of your pleasure.)
The second aspect is that they indicate exhortation, in which case they are specific to verbal sentences, as in «لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة».

dervis-irab:45-50.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غِلٍّ): al-ghill, with kasra on the ghayn, is rancour hidden in the heart, from inghalla fī jawfihi and taghalghala "it penetrated deep inside him"; it is applied to ill-will, enmity, hatred, rancour and envy. You say: "Allah put a burning thirst (ghulla) in his liver, a ghill in his chest, shackles (ghulūl) on his property and a ghull on his neck"; al-ghull, with ḍamma, is the fetter. It is a root that indicates penetration deep within, matching its sound; one says "a burning passion penetrates deep into my entrails (taghalghala)", and "he delivered to so-and-so a mughalghala", which is a message arriving from a distant land, and "I sent a message to him (ghalghaltu)". Al-Akhṭal said:
لأغلغلن إلى كريم مدحة ... ولأثنينّ بنائل وفعال
(I will surely send a praise-poem deep to a noble man, and I will surely extol him for his generosity and deeds.)

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ) إن and its noun; في جنات is its predicate; and عيون is conjoined to جنات. (ادْخُلُوها بِسَلامٍ آمِنِينَ) The clause is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "it will be said to them"; ادخلوها is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; بسلام is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the wāw in ادخلوها, i.e. "safe from every harm", or "being greeted with peace"; and آمنين is a second ḥāl from the wāw in ادخلوها. (وَنَزَعْنا ما فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ إِخْواناً عَلى سُرُرٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ) ونزعنا is a verb and agent; ما is the direct object; في صدورهم is the ṣila; من غل is a ḥāl of clarification (ḥāl bayān) for what had settled in their breasts; إخوانا is a second ḥāl from هم; على سرر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to متقابلين; and متقابلين is a third ḥāl from the pronoun of صدورهم, and this is permissible because the muḍāf is a part of the muḍāf ilayhi, and the operator in it is the sense of attachment. It was also said that متقابلين is an adjective of إخوانا, and that is not far-fetched, but the first is preferable: that is, none of them looks at the back of another's neck, since the couches turn with them, and this is the manner of those seated at drinking tables and banquets, because that is more complete in intimacy and honouring. (لا يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيها نَصَبٌ وَما هُمْ مِنْها بِمُخْرَجِينَ) This clause may be resumptive or a ḥāl from the pronoun in متقابلين; لا is negative; يمسهم is an imperfect verb with a fronted direct object; نصب is a postponed agent; وما هم: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Ḥijāzī negative; هم is its noun; منها is attached to بمخرجين; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and مخرجين is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the khabar of ما. (نَبِّئْ عِبادِي أَنِّي أَنَا الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ) نبىء is an imperative verb and the agent is latent; عبادي is a direct object; أن and what is in its scope take the place of the objects of نبىء; أن and its noun; أنا is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; الغفور is the khabar of أن, or the khabar of أنا with the clause being the khabar of أن; and الرحيم is a second khabar. (وَأَنَّ عَذابِي هُوَ الْعَذابُ الْأَلِيمُ) It is conjoined to the preceding and the parsing is the same, except that الأليم is an adjective of العذاب.

* Benefits:
His words «نبىء عبادي اني أنا الغفور الرحيم» are among what occurs in the Qurʾān in metrical form, yet it is not poetry because it is not intended as such. We have already spoken of some verses that came out measured, and this verse forms a complete line of the baḥr al-mujtathth. But there we did not mention the meanings of the names of the metres, so here is an account of the names and their meanings:
Al-Zajjāj mentioned that Ibn Durayd informed him, from Abū Ḥātim, from al-Akhfash, who said:
I asked al-Khalīl: "Why was al-ṭawīl called ṭawīl?" He said: "Because it is long (ṭāla) by the completeness of its parts." I said: "And al-basīṭ?" He said: "Because it extends (inbasaṭa) beyond the span of al-ṭawīl, its middle being faʿilun and its end faʿilun." I said: "And al-madīd?" He said: "Because its seven-letter feet are stretched (tamaddud) around its five-letter feet." I said: "And al-wāfir?" He said: "Because of the abundance (wufūr) of its parts, peg upon peg." I said: "And al-kāmil?"
He said: "Because it has thirty vowelled letters that do not combine in any other poetry." I said: "And al-hazaj?"
He said: "Because it is shaky (yaḍṭarib), resembling the hazaj of a voice (its trilling)." I said: "And al-rajaz?" He said: "Because of its tremor, like the tremor of a she-camel's legs when she stands." I said: "And al-ramal?" He said: "Because it is like the weaving (ramal) of a mat, with parts joined to one another." I said: "And al-sarīʿ?" He said: "Because it moves swiftly (yusriʿ) on the tongue." I said: "And al-munsariḥ?" He said: "For its fluency and ease." I said: "And al-khafīf?"
He said: "Because it is the lightest of the seven-letter metres." I said: "And al-muqtaḍab?" He said: "Because it was cut off (iqtuḍiba) from al-sarīʿ." I said: "And al-muḍāriʿ?" He said: "Because it resembles (ḍāraʿa) al-muqtaḍab." I said:
"And al-mujtathth?" He said: "Because it was uprooted (ijtutha), that is, cut off from the circle of al-ṭawīl." I said:
"And al-mutaqārib?" He said: "For the closeness (taqārub) of its parts, because they are all five-letter feet resembling one another."

dervis-irab:51-64.t:
* I'rab:
(وَنَبِّئْهُمْ عَنْ ضَيْفِ إِبْراهِيمَ) It is conjoined to نبىء عبادي, so that they may take a lesson from what befell the people of Lūṭ of punishment. ونبئهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; and عن ضيف ابراهيم is attached to نبئهم. The origin of الضيف is a maṣdar, and for that reason the singular and the plural are alike in it, although it may be pluralised, so one says aḍyāf, ḍuyūf and ḍayfān.
(إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقالُوا سَلاماً قالَ إِنَّا مِنْكُمْ وَجِلُونَ) The adverb is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; the clause دخلوا is annexed to it; عليه is attached to دخلوا; فقالوا is conjoined to دخلوا; سلاما is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. "we greet with a greeting", or a direct object in sense, i.e. "mention a greeting"; قال is a past verb; the clause إنا etc. is the content of the saying; إن and its noun; منكم is attached to وجلون; and وجلون is the khabar of إنا, i.e. "afraid", either because they refrained from eating or because they entered without permission.
(قالُوا لا تَوْجَلْ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ) لا is prohibitive; توجل is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا; إن and its noun; the clause نبشرك is its khabar; بغلام is attached to نبشرك; عليم is an adjective; and the clause is causal for the absence of fear. (قالَ أَبَشَّرْتُمُونِي عَلى أَنْ مَسَّنِيَ الْكِبَرُ فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ) The hamza is for an interrogative of astonishment; بشرتموني is a verb, agent and direct object; على is a preposition; أن and what is in its scope are in the position of genitive after على, and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "while old age has touched me"; الكبر is the agent of مسني; فبم: the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun whose alif was dropped because of the entry of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تبشرون.
(قالُوا بَشَّرْناكَ بِالْحَقِّ فَلا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْقانِطِينَ) The clause بشرناك is the content of the saying, and it is a past verb, agent and direct object; بالحق is attached to بشرناك; the fāʾ is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تكن is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا, and the noun of تكن is latent, its implied form being "you"; and من القانطين is its khabar. (قالَ وَمَنْ يَقْنَطُ مِنْ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّهِ إِلَّا الضَّالُّونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; من is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause يقنط is its khabar; من رحمة ربه is attached to يقنط; إلا is a particle of restriction; and الضالون is a substitute for the latent pronoun in يقنط, a partial substitute (badal baʿḍ min kull), and no pronoun is brought with it because of the strong attachment of the excepted to the one excepted from. (قالَ فَما خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, so that the dialogue may be consistent; ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; خطبكم is the khabar, i.e. "what is your business"; أيها is an indefinite vocative made specific, the particle of vocative being omitted, and the hāʾ is for attention; and المرسلون is a substitute or an adjective of أيها. (قالُوا إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنا إِلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ)
إن and its noun; the clause أرسلنا is its khabar; نا is the deputy agent of أرسل; إلى قوم is attached to أرسلنا; and مجرمين is an adjective. (إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ إِنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) There are two views on it. The first is that it is a connected exception, excepted from the latent pronoun in مجرمين, the meaning being that they all offended except the family of Lūṭ, who did not offend; and on this view the clause إنا لمنجوهم is resumptive, brought to report their deliverance because they did not offend. The second is that it is a disconnected exception, because the family of Lūṭ were not included at all among the offenders. On either view its position is accusative. It appears that making it disconnected is preferable and more feasible, because excepting them from the pronoun referring to "a people of offenders" is remote, in that the place of exception is to remove what would, but for the exception, have entered the ruling of the first; and this entering is precluded by the indefiniteness, which is why you rarely find an indefinite noun being excepted from except in a context of negation, since then it is more general and the entering would be realised were it not for the exception. Hence it is not good to say "I saw a people except Zayd", while it is good to say "I did not see anyone except Zayd". إن and its noun; the shifted lām; منجوهم is the khabar of إنا; and أجمعين is an emphasis of the pronoun. On this view the clause إنا لمنجوهم is connected with آل لوط, as though it were the khabar of an implied لكن, i.e. "but the family of Lūṭ are to be saved". (إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْنا إِنَّها لَمِنَ الْغابِرِينَ) The parsers differed regarding this exception, and we shall quote what al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
"If you say: 'His words إلا امرأته — from what is it excepted? Is it an exception from an exception?' I say: it is excepted from the genitive pronoun in His words لمنجوهم, and it is nothing of an exception from an exception, because an exception from an exception occurs only where the ruling is one and the same, and where it is said 'We destroyed them except the family of Lūṭ except his wife', as the ruling is one in the saying of the divorcer 'You are divorced three except two except one', and in the saying of the one making an acknowledgement 'So-and-so has ten dirhams against me except three except one dirham'. As for the verse, the two rulings differ, because إلا آل لوط is attached to أرسلنا or to مجرمين, while إلا امرأته is attached to منجوهم, so how could it be an exception from an exception?"
And Abū al-Baqāʾ said: His words, the Exalted, إلا امرأته have two views. One is that it is excepted from آل لوط, and when an exception comes after an exception the second exception is annexed to the mubtadaʾ, as in your saying "he has ten with me except four, not one dirham", for the dirham is excepted from the four and so is annexed to the ten, as if you had said "eleven except four" or "ten except three". The second view is that it is excepted from the pronoun of the object in منجوهم, and more will come under Benefits.
قدرنا is a verb and agent, and it has been made to contain the sense of knowing, so it is suspended by the lām and the kasra of إن is used. The angels ascribed the decree to themselves because of their standing and nearness to Allah, as the king's close associates say "we commanded and we decreed", although they commanded and decreed by the king's command. إن and its noun; the shifted lām; and من الغابرين is the khabar of إن. (فَلَمَّا جاءَ آلَ لُوطٍ الْمُرْسَلُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted clause, i.e. "so they left his presence and travelled to the town of the people of Lūṭ"; لما is temporal or connective; جاء is a past verb; آل لوط is a fronted direct object; and المرسلون is a postponed agent. (قالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ) The clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; إن with its noun and khabar; and منكرون is an adjective of قوم. (قالُوا: بَلْ جِئْناكَ بِما كانُوا فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ) بل is a particle of exchange and conjunction; جئناك is a verb, agent and direct object; بما is attached to جئناك; the clause كانوا is a ṣila; فيه is attached to يمترون; and the clause يمترون is the khabar of كانوا.
(وَأَتَيْناكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّا لَصادِقُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أتيناك is a verb, agent and direct object; بالحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being accompanied by it", or "you being accompanied by it" for your seeing it, and it may be attached to آتيناك; إن and its noun; the shifted lām; and صادقون is the khabar of إن.

* Benefits:
We came across a debate that took place between al-Kisāʾī and Abū Yūsuf regarding His words, the Exalted, «إلا امرأته» and the ruling on «إلا» when repeated. Al-Kisāʾī asked Abū Yūsuf about one who said: "He has a hundred dirhams against me except ten except two." He said:
"Eighty-eight is obligatory upon him." Al-Kisāʾī said: "Rather, ninety-two is obligatory upon him," and he adduced the verse as evidence, and Abū Yūsuf did not disagree with him. This supports the view of Abū al-Baqāʾ and shows the saying of al-Zamakhsharī to be mistaken. Ibn Hishām said: "Its like is His words, the Exalted, «إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين إلا آل لوط إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين إلا امرأته»: the woman is excepted from the first, and the family are excepted from the people of offenders, which is disconnected, while the second is connected; so it appeared to me. Moreover, in a case such as 'ten except four except two' I do not consider it impossible that the two be excepted from the original, because reading it to the nearest is more probable, not obligatory, and the chapter of tanāzuʿ (competing operators) is sufficient witness, since each of the two parties permits each of the two operators to operate except what is excluded by some accident, and the accident is found here as well, as in 'ten except three except four'. If you say: What prevents the second exception in the verse from being from the people of offenders, and its connectedness supports this view too, because she is of the family and of the offenders? I say: whoever says this has gone far and spoken absurdly. As for the first, it is plain; as for the second, because the meaning of 'we were sent' is with punishment, so it is not sound to remove her from those punished. If you say: What prevents her being excepted from the 'them' in إنا لمنجوهم, in which case she would be punished, and it would be a reading to the nearest of what I mentioned, and the verse would leave the category of exception from an exception? I say: that is the saying of al-Zamakhsharī, and with me it is not like most of his parsing statements, because «إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين» was mentioned only for emphasis, not as a new statement, since its meaning is derived from the removal from the ruling of those punished."
After quoting the above, I found a fine objection, which is that it has gone before that what is meant by offending is that heinous deed; so how can they say the woman is of the family and of the offenders, when that deed cannot be imagined from her? On this basis both opinions fall. It may be answered that pointing to a thing is like doing it, or that remaining silent about the offence and being content with it is itself an offence. We have prolonged the discussion only because this verse is one on which much has been said, and few of the great authorities hit the mark. Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī was asked about it in the Fatāwā and did not reach the aim. And Allah knows best.
Abū Ḥayyān was inconsistent in his discussion of the two views and in weighing them, saying:
"Since al-Zamakhsharī took as given that «إلا امرأته» is excepted from the genitive pronoun in لمنجوهم, he did not allow it to be an exception from an exception. As for whoever says it is an exception from an exception, his statement can be made sound in one of two ways. One is that since the pronoun in لمنجوهم refers to the family of Lūṭ, and the woman has been excepted from it, it is as though she were excepted from the family of Lūṭ, because the pronoun is, in meaning, the overt noun. The other is that His words «إلا آل لوط», when they were given a ruling different from that on 'a people of offenders', required their deliverance, so that His words «إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين» came as an emphasis of the meaning of the exception, since the meaning is 'except the family of Lūṭ, to whom no punishment was sent'.
