So it became like your saying 'the people stood except Zayd', for he did not stand, or 'except Zayd, he did not stand'; this clause is an emphasis of what the exception contains, namely a ruling on what follows إلا opposite to the ruling preceding the excepted-from. So «إلا امرأته», on the analysis we have set out, is an exception from the family of Lūṭ, because an exception from what is brought as a new statement is better than one from what is brought as an emphasis."

dervis-irab:12-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَسْلُكُهُ): we make it enter. One says salaktu the thread in the needle and aslaktuhu when you made it enter it. In al-Mukhtār: "al-silk with kasra is the thread, and with fatḥa it is the verbal noun of salaka al-shayʾ fī al-shayʾ, so insalaka, that is, he made it enter and it entered. Its pattern is naṣara. Allah the Exalted said: «كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين»; and aslaka is a dialectal variant of it." In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: salaka yasluku (with ḍamma on the lām in the imperfect), salkan and sulūkan: the place, he entered it; and the road, he travelled it following it; aslaka the thing in the thing: he made it enter, as the thread is passed into the needle; salakahu the place, aslakahu the place, and fīhi and ʿalayhi: he made it enter.
(سُكِّرَتْ): bewildered, or restrained, of sights, or blocked. One says sakartu the river sakran (pattern qatala) when you dammed it, and al-sikr with kasra is what is used to dam it. In al-Qāmūs and its commentary and others: sakara yaskuru the vessel sakran (pattern qatala): he filled it; the river: he made a dam for it; the door: he shut it. Sakarat the wind sukūran and sakarānan: it grew still; and the heat: it slackened and sakara. Sukkira his sight: he was bewildered and kept from looking. Sakira yaskaru (pattern ʿalima) the pool: it was filled. Sakira the man ʿalayhi: he was enraged and angry. And sakira sakran, sakran, sukran and sakarānan from drink is the opposite of ṣaḥā (being sober), so he is sakir and sakrān, and she is sakra, sakrā and sakrāna, and the plural sakrā, sakārā and sukārā. For the sīn with the kāf, when they occur as the first and second radicals of the verb, there is the meaning of affecting a thing and producing an effect in it. One says sakaba the water: he poured it out and shed it, and water and blood are askūb (flowing). Janūb, sister of ʿAmr Dhū al-Kalb, said:
الطاعن الطعنة النجلاء يتبعها ... مثعنجر من دم الأجواف أسكوب
(He who thrusts the wide spear-wound, followed by a gushing flow of blood from the innards.)
And "this is an amr sakb" and "a sunna sakb": a binding obligation. Laqīṭ ibn Zurāra said to his brother Maʿbad, when he had been captured and had asked him to ransom him with two hundred camels: "I will not give (munṭin, that is, muʿṭin) anything on your behalf that would become a binding custom (sunnatan sakban) upon your household, so that people become used to us through it." And sakata the man: an illness struck him that prevented him from speech; a man is sakūt, sākūt and sikkīt, and he has sakāt if he is long silent from illness; and for the pregnant woman there is a cry and then a silence (sakta). Figuratively: "I struck him until I silenced (askattu) his movement". Al-sakta is a known illness by which the limbs are disabled from feeling and movement except breathing; and al-sakta is what remains in the vessel and what one quiets a child or other with; and al-sakāt is a sickness that prevents (harm) from snakes, and al-sakāt among snakes is one that stings before one perceives it. Sakaʿa yaskaʿu (patterns fahima and fataḥa) sakʿan and sakaʿan: he walked without guidance because of being affected; "so-and-so yatasakkaʿu": he does not know where on Allah's earth he is heading; and tasakkaʿa in darkness: he stumbled about in it. He said:
أيادي بيضا بيّضت وجه مطلبي ... وقد كنت في ظلمائه أتسكع
(Bright favours whitened the face of my aim, when I had been wandering aimlessly in its darkness.)
One of the Arabs was asked about His saying the Exalted «في طغيانهم يعمهون», and he said: "In their wandering they stumble (yatasakkaʿūn)." And iskāf, with kasra on the hamza, from al-asākifa, is the cobbler (kharrāz), and it is said: any craftsman; and "I did not tread the threshold (uskuffa) of his door", "I did not frequent (tasakkaftu) his door", and "by Allah I will not make for him a threshold at any house"; and figuratively: "the tear stopped on the threshold of his eye", that is, on its lower lid. Sakka the door: he sealed it with iron; sakka the well: he dug it; sakka his ears: he cut them off; sakka the ostrich what is in its belly: it cast it out thin. It is said: "that speech did not sakka my hearing", that is, did not enter it; "this dirham was struck in the mint (sikka) of so-and-so"; "he split the earth with the plough-share (sikka)"; "he has a row (sikka) of palm trees"; and "he lives in the lane (sikka) of Banū So-and-so", which is the wide alley. Figuratively: istakkat masāmiʿuhu: his hearing was stopped up. Al-Nābigha said:
أتاني أبيت اللعين أنك لمتني ... وتلك التي تستك منها المسامع
(It came to me, may you refuse curses, that you blamed me, and that is something at which ears are stopped up.)
And "the moving thing came to rest (sakana)", and "I stilled it (askantuhu) and quietened it (sakkantuhu)", and "its movements and stillnesses were proportioned"; "they dwelt in the house (sakanū al-dār)" and "they dwelt in it", and "I settled them in the house (askantuhum al-dār) and in it". Figuratively: "my soul grew still (sakanat nafsī) after agitation", and "I taught him knowledge to which the soul is at rest (sakanat ilayhi)", and "mā lī sakan", that is, one to whom I may turn for rest, such as a wife or a close friend. Abū al-Ṭayyib said:
بم التعلل لا أهل ولا وطن ... ولا نديم ولا كأس ولا سكن
(With what is there solace, when there is no family, no homeland, no boon companion, no cup and no comforting presence?)
And "upon him is serenity (sakīna), dignity and composure"; and "they have a blow that removes the heads from their resting-places (sakanāt)". Al-Nābigha said:
بضرب يزيل الهام عن سكناته ... وطعن كايزاغ المخاض الضوارب
(With a blow that removes heads from their resting-places, and a thrust like the spurting of pregnant she-camels in labour.)
And this, as it seems, is more likely to have been intended; but our language was born with inspiration, keeping pace with the thoughts of the souls and their whisperings.
(بُرُوجاً): the plural of burj. The signs (burūj) of the sky are twelve, as they used to say: Aries (al-ḥamal), Taurus (al-thawr), Gemini (al-jawzāʾ), Cancer (al-saraṭān), Leo (al-asad), Virgo (al-sunbula), Libra (al-mīzān), Scorpio (al-ʿaqrab), Sagittarius (al-qaws), Capricorn (al-jadī), Aquarius (al-dalw) and Pisces (al-ḥūt). They said they are the mansions of the seven wandering planets: Mars (al-Mirrīkh), whose mansions are Aries and Scorpio; Venus (al-Zuhra), whose are Taurus and Libra; Mercury (ʿUṭārid, which is a diptote because of the form of the extreme plurals), whose are Gemini and Virgo; the Moon, whose is Cancer; the Sun, whose is Leo; Jupiter (al-Mushtarī), whose are Sagittarius and Pisces; and Saturn (Zuḥal, a diptote because of being a proper name and ʿadl, like ʿUmar), whose are Capricorn and Aquarius. We have not given these names as scientific verification, for science has changed much of this elementary information and has discovered what never crossed the mind or reckoning; we have given them only for the linguistic benefits.
(اسْتَرَقَ): he snatched it and stole it; sāraqahu al-naẓar is the same; and "the scribe istaraqa some of the accounts" when he did not bring them out.
(شِهابٌ): al-shihāb is anything luminous generated from fire, and what is seen as though it were a star that has fallen, and a star in general, and the spearhead because of the gleam in it; the plural is shuhub. Abū Tammām said, using paronomasia:
والعلم في شهب الأرماح ساطعة ... بين الخمسين لا في السبعة الشهب
(Knowledge shines in the gleaming spears between the two fifties, not in the seven shuhb.) [Translator's note: the verse is rendered as written in the source; the pun on shuhb (gleaming spearheads / planets) is not reproducible in English.]
(مَعايِشَ): the plural of maʿīsha, which is what a person lives by during the span of his life, of foods, drinks and clothing. It is with a true yāʾ, unlike al-shamāʾil and al-khabāʾith, because the yāʾ in maʿāyish is original in the singular, and a long vowel in the singular is not turned into a hamza in the plural unless it is an addition in the singular, as Ibn Mālik said in al-Khulāṣa:
والمد زيد ثالثا في الواحد ... همزا يرى في مثل كالقلائد
(A madd added as third letter in the singular is seen as a hamza in the like of "al-qalāʾid".)

* I'rab:
(كَذلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "like that insertion we insert it into the hearts of the criminals"; نسلكه is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; and في قلوب المجرمين is attached to نسلكه.
(لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ سُنَّةُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl, and it may be explicative of His saying نسلكه and so have no grammatical position; يؤمنون is an imperfect verb and agent; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنون; وقد: the wāw is circumstantial and قد is a particle of affirmation; خلت سنة الأولين is a verb and fāʿil, and the clause is circumstantial; it is possible that the wāw is resumptive and the clause resumptive, that is, "the way of Allah in destroying and punishing them has passed." (وَلَوْ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ باباً مِنَ السَّماءِ فَظَلُّوا فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; لو is the conditional of impossibility; فتحنا is a verb and agent; عليهم is attached to فتحنا; بابا is a direct object; من السماء is an adjective of بابا; the fāʾ is a conjunction; ظل and its ism (the mention of the pronoun in يعرجون will come in the chapter on rhetoric); فيه is attached to يعرجون; and the clause يعرجون is the khabar of ظل. (لَقالُوا إِنَّما سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصارُنا بَلْ نَحْنُ قَوْمٌ مَسْحُورُونَ) The lām occurs in the answer to لو; قالوا is a verb and agent; إنما is kāffa and makfūfa; سكرت أبصارنا is a verb and fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to لو; the clause إنما سكرت أبصارنا is the quoted speech; the clause نحن قوم مسحورون is subordinate to the clause سكرت أبصارنا; بل is a particle of retraction; نحن is a mubtadaʾ; قوم is the khabar; and مسحورون is an adjective. (وَلَقَدْ جَعَلْنا فِي السَّماءِ بُرُوجاً وَزَيَّنَّاها لِلنَّاظِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; جعلنا is a verb and agent; if it means "we created", then His words في السماء are attached to it, and if it means "we made", then its first object is بروجا and the preposition and its genitive noun, in the position of the accusative, are the second object; زيناها is a verb, an agent and a direct object; and للناظرين is attached to زيناها. (وَحَفِظْناها مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطانٍ رَجِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; حفظناها is a verb, agent and direct object; من كل شيطان رجيم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حفظناها; and رجيم is an adjective of شيطان.
(إِلَّا مَنِ اسْتَرَقَ السَّمْعَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهابٌ مُبِينٌ) إلا is a particle of exception; من is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) if "guarding" is interpreted as prevention, that is, the prevention of the devils from approaching it at all and from standing upon what is in it in general; or a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) if it is interpreted as prevention from entering it and from acting in it.
The fāʾ is a conjunction; أتبعه is a past verb and direct object; شهاب is the fāʿil; and مبين is an adjective.
(وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْناها وَأَلْقَيْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ) والأرض is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation), that is, a direct object of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; مددناها is a verb, agent and direct object; ألقينا is a verb and agent; فيها is attached to ألقينا; and رواسي is a direct object, that is, "firm mountains", lest it sway with its people. (وَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْزُونٍ) وأنبتنا is conjoined to what precedes; فيها is attached to أنبتنا; من كل شيء is an adjective of the omitted direct object, that is, "plants of every thing"; and موزون is an adjective, that is, whose measure is known. (وَجَعَلْنا لَكُمْ فِيها مَعايِشَ وَمَنْ لَسْتُمْ لَهُ بِرازِقِينَ) وجعلنا is conjoined to what precedes; لكم is attached to جعلنا or is in the position of the second object; فيها is a ḥāl; معايش is the object of جعلنا; and the relative من is conjoined to معايش or to the position of لكم, as if it were said "and We made for you in it livelihoods, and We made for you those whom you do not provide for", or "and We made for you in it livelihoods, and for those whom you do not provide for". By them He meant dependants, servants, retinue and beasts. Al-Zajjāj implied it as accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "and We enriched those whom you do not provide for". It is also possible to cut off the wāw so that it is a commencing wāw and من a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "and for those whom you do not provide for We made livelihoods in it".

* Rhetoric:
In His saying the Exalted «كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين، لا يؤمنون به وقد خلت سنة الأولين، ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلوا فيه يعرجون، لقالوا إنما سكرت أبصارنا بل نحن قوم مسحورون» there is an allegorical simile (tashbīh tamthīlī) of the obstinacy that has overtaken them and the deep-rooted stubbornness in their breasts. The detail of that is that Allah the Exalted inserted the Qur'an into their hearts and made it enter the very core of them, as He inserted it into the hearts of the believers who affirm its truth; so these denied it and those affirmed it, each with knowledge and clear proof, so that whoever perishes may perish with a clear proof and whoever lives may live with a clear proof, and so that the disbelievers may have no argument against Allah that they did not understand the aspects of its inimitability as the one who believed understood them. So Allah the Exalted informed them from now, while they have respite and opportunity, that they disbelieved only knowingly, obstinately and wrongfully, so as to be a more decisive refutation of any argument they may fabricate and a cleaner rejection of every claim they conjecture. Therefore Allah the Exalted followed it with His saying «ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلوا فيه يعرجون لقالوا» etc., meaning that these people understood the Qur'an with true understanding, grasped its secrets, plumbed the depths of its miracles, knew the aspects of its inimitability, and it penetrated to the depths of their souls and settled in their ears; but they are a people whose habit is obstinacy and whose disposition is contentiousness and defiance, so that even if the clearest of paths, those most compelling to belief by the necessity of sight and witnessing, were opened to them, namely that a door be opened for them in the heaven through which they would ascend and be made to ascend until they entered it in daytime -- and He pointed to that with His word ظلوا, since ẓulūl occurs only in the day -- they would say, after this great and unveiled clarification, "only our sight has been dazzled and Muḥammad has bewitched us, and these are only deceptive illusions with no realities beneath them." So He recorded against them that they have no excuse in their denial, as if it were from lack of hearing, awareness, arrival at the hearts and understanding as others who affirmed the truth understood, because their way is to persist in stubbornness, obduracy, defiance and contentiousness. If we move to the detail, we say in this allegorical simile:
1- Completion (al-tatmīm), which has been mentioned before, through presenting the various fields of observation and consideration.
2- Precaution (al-iḥtirās) in the word ظلوا, lest their ascent be in the dark, so that they would take it as an excuse for not being guided.
3- The dazzling (sukr) of the eyes by way of the implicit, derivative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-tabaʿiyya).
4- In the two words of restriction and retraction is an indication of the decisive judgment that what they see has no reality but is falsehood imagined to them by a kind of magic, according to their claim. The explanation is that they said «إنما», which gives restriction to what is mentioned last, so the restriction is on the eyes, not on the dazzling; as if they said: "our eyes have been dazzled, not our minds, and although we imagine these things with these eyes, we know with our minds that the matter is otherwise, that is, that it has no reality." Then they said «بل», as if they retracted from the restriction to the eyes and said: rather it went beyond that to our minds, by a magic he worked upon us.
These verses are among the marvels before which eloquence stands in submission.

dervis-irab:21-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَواقِحَ): pregnant, because they carry the clouds and stir them up. There are two views on it. One is that it is the plural of lāqiḥ, when it brings good by producing rain-bearing clouds, just as the one that brings no good is called a barren (ʿaqīm) wind. The second is that it has the meaning of malāqiḥ, which are the females with young in their bellies. The poet said:
ليبك يزيد ضارع لخصومة ... ومختبط ممّا تطيح الطوائح
(Let one humbled by a dispute weep for Yazīd, and one who seeks his bounty, for what the destroyers cast away.)
He means al-maṭāwiḥ, the plural of muṭīḥa. Its verb is laqiḥa: one says laqiḥat talqaḥu (pattern taʿiba) laqḥan, laqaḥan and liqāḥan: the she-camel or the like received the stud or conceived, so she is lāqiḥ and laqūḥ; laqiḥat the war: it flared up after calm; and laqiḥat the woman: she conceived.
What follows are the sayings of the great linguists:
Abū ʿUbayda said: al-lawāqiḥ is the plural of mulqiḥ, because it is from alqaḥa yulqiḥu, so he is mulqiḥ, and its plural is malāqiḥ, and the mīm was dropped for lightness. One says alqaḥat al-rīḥ the clouds, as one says alqaḥa the stallion the female.
Al-Azharī said: al-lawāqiḥ is the plural of lāqiḥ. One says laqiḥat the wind when it carried water, so they are bearers because they bear the clouds, like your saying alqaḥtu the she-camel and so she conceived (laqiḥat) when she carried the foetus in her belly; the wind was likened to it.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-lawāqiḥ is the plural of lāqiḥ on the nisba pattern like labbān and tāmir, that is, possessor of laqāḥ.
And in al-Mukhtār: "Alqaḥa the stallion the she-camel, and the wind the clouds; and riyāḥ lawāqiḥ, and do not say malāqiḥ."

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا عِنْدَنا خَزائِنُهُ) إن is negative; من in شيء is redundant in the mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; the adverb عندنا is attached to an omitted preposed khabar; خزائنه is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is the khabar of شيء. (وَما نُنَزِّلُهُ إِلَّا بِقَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; ننزله is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; بقدر is a ḥāl from the object, that is, "accompanied by a measure", and you may attach it to ننزله; and معلوم is an adjective of قدر. (وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّياحَ لَواقِحَ) وأرسلنا الرياح is a verb, agent and direct object; and لواقح is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from الرياح. (فَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَسْقَيْناكُمُوهُ وَما أَنْتُمْ لَهُ بِخازِنِينَ) فأنزلنا: the fāʾ is a conjunction and أنزلنا is conjoined to أرسلنا; من السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلنا; ماء is a direct object; فأسقيناكموه: the fāʾ is a conjunction; أسقى is a past verb; نا is the fāʿil; the kāf is the first object; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural; the wāw is for the lengthening of the ḍamma of the mīm; and the hāʾ is the second object. وما: the wāw is circumstantial and ما is a negative of Ḥijāzī type; أنتم is its ism; له is attached to خازنين; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and خازنين is the khabar of ما, genitive in position, by the bāʾ in form. (وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَنَحْنُ الْوارِثُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن with its ism; the shifted lām; نحن is a mubtadaʾ and the clause نحيي is its khabar; it is possible that نحن is an emphasis of نا, and it is not permissible that it be a separating pronoun, because it did not occur between two nouns; ونحن is a mubtadaʾ and الوارثون the khabar. (وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا الْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنْكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا الْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; علمنا is a verb and agent; المستقدمين is a direct object; منكم is a ḥāl; and ولقد علمنا المستأخرين is a conjunction. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ إِنَّهُ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ) وإن ربك: إن with its ism; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يحشرهم its khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of إن; إن with its ism; حكيم is a first khabar and عليم a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- The allegorical metaphor in His saying «وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه»: He likened what all servants benefit from, not rain alone as some said, to the treasuries in which hidden and stored things are deposited, to bring out each thing according to what divine wisdom requires and the vital interests of the servants.
2- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya) in likening the winds to the lawāqiḥ, which are she-camels, for the generation of rain, a matter on which the discourse has been extensively set out and which does not conflict with this metaphor.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوْ كَانُواْ مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ ("perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims"). It may be asked: how did rubba enter upon an action that had not happened, since the wishing of those who disbelieve will only be in the Hereafter? It is answered: the Qurʾān was sent down — its promise, its threat and whatever is in it — as truth, so it is as something seen; hence speech about what has not yet happened of it ran the same course as about what has happened. Do you not see His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهِمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ ("if you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord"), and His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إذْ فَزِعُوا﴾ ("if you could see when they are terrified") — as though it were past, while it is awaited, because of its truth in meaning? And a speaker, when he forbids or commands and the one commanded disobeys him, says: "By Allah, many a regret (la-rubba nadāmatin) will be yours in which you will remember my words", because he knows that he will regret it. [Al-Farrāʾ] says: and the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is truer than the saying of created beings.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ﴾ ("We never destroyed a town except that it had a known decree"). Had there been no wāw in it, it would be correct, as He said in another place: ﴿وَمَا أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلاّ لَهَا مُنْذِرُونَ﴾ ("We never destroyed a town except that it had warners"). It is as you say in speech: "I saw no one except that he had clothes on (illā wa-ʿalayhi thiyāb)", or if you wish: "illā ʿalayhi thiyāb". So with every indefinite noun whose predication comes after illā while the statement about the indefinite is complete: do that with its ṣila after illā. But if what falls upon the indefinite is incomplete, it can only be by dropping the wāw. Of that is: "I do not think any dirham but sufficient for you (illā kāfiyaka)", and "illā wa-huwa kāfīka" is not permissible, because ẓann ("thinking") needs two things, so you do not interpose the wāw, which would make ẓann like verbs that are satisfied with one noun. Likewise the sisters of ẓanantu, and kāna and its like, and inna and its sisters (and inna): when the verb comes after (إلاّ) there is no wāw in it. So it is wrong to say: "Inna a man, while he is standing", or "I think a man, while he is standing", or "No man was, except while he was standing".
It is permissible with laysa specifically to say: "There is no one but that he is thus (illā wa-huwa hākadhā)", because the statement may be imagined complete with laysa and an indefinite word — do you not see that you say: "laysa aḥadun" and "mā min aḥadin"? — so that is permissible with it, but not with aẓunnu; do you not see that you do not say: "I do not think anyone"? The poet said:

إِذا ما سُتورُ البيت أُرخِين لم يكن * سراج لنا إلاّ وَوَجهُك أنور
(Whenever the curtains of the house are let down, we have no lamp but your face is brighter.)

Had it been said "illā wajhuka anwar" it would be correct.
And another said:

وما مَسّ كفّى من يد طاب ريحها * منَ الناس إلاّ ريحُ كفَّيك أطيب
(My palm has touched no fragrant hand among people but the scent of your palms is sweeter.)

So he came with the wāw and without the wāw. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِنَ المُرْسَلِين إلا إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعام﴾ ("We sent no messengers before you except that they ate food"): in this place, had there been a wāw, it would be proper. When you bring a negation into kāna, what comes after illā is proper with it both with and without wāw. And when you bring in an interrogative intending negation by it, both the wāw and its dropping are proper after illā, as you say: "Was there anyone but that he had (illā wa-lahu) a greed for this world?" and "illā lahu a greed for this world".
As for aṣbaḥa, amsā and raʾaytu, the wāw is easier with them, because they are / [ms. 91a] complete (tawāmm, meaning tāmmāt) in one state, while kāna, laysa and aẓunnu are built on incompleteness. You may say: "There is no one but that he has a livelihood (illā wa-lahu maʿāsh)", and if you drop the wāw it is correct, because you say "laysa aḥadun" and stop, and it is a [complete] statement. Likewise lā of total exclusion (al-tabriʾa) and others: you say "lā rajula" and "lā min rajulin"; in what refers back to it after illā, the wāw and its absence are both permissible, given completeness. That is not permissible with aẓunnu, because ẓann by its nature admits of being cancelled (ilghāʾ): do you not see that you say "Zayd is standing, I think"? The entry of "I think" is for doubt, so it is as though it were dispensable; whereas [negation] is not a negation [Translator's note: so in the text: «وليس بنفى»; the sense appears to be "whereas it is not so with negation"], and the statement is not independent of the negation, because you only give the report as being so or not being so; so it is not said of negation that it is superfluous in speech, as it is said of ẓann.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا تَسْبِقُ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلَهَا وَمَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ﴾ ("no nation can advance its term, nor do they delay it"). He did not say tastaʾkhiru, because the word umma is feminine in form; so the beginning of the expression was brought out in accordance with its femininity, and its end in accordance with the meaning of men. Similar to it is ﴿كلَّمَا جَاءَ أُمةً رَسُولُهَا كذَّبُوهُ﴾ ("whenever its messenger came to a nation, they denied him"); had it been said kadhdhabathu it would be correct. This is frequent.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا﴾ ("why do you not bring us…?"). Lawlā and lawmā are two dialectal forms, used in statement and in question. As for the statement, it is His saying: ﴿لَوْلا أَنتَمْ لكُنَّا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ("were it not for you, we would have been believers").
And the poet said:

* لوما هوَى عِرْسِ كُمَيت لم أُبَل *
(Were it not for love of the bride of Kumayt, I would not care.)

Both of them put what follows them in the nominative.
As for the question, it is His saying: ﴿لَّوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا بِٱلْمَلائِكَةِ﴾ ("why do you not bring us the angels?"), and His saying: ﴿لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنىِ إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾ ("if only You would delay me for a short term"), the meaning — and Allah knows best — being: "why did You not delay me?"
The Arabs have used (لولا) in statements, and speech with it became so frequent that they allowed themselves to say lawlāka and lawlāya, the meaning in both being as in your saying lawlā anā and lawlā anta. The kāf is sometimes taken as genitive, but the nominative is correct for it. That is because we have not found any overt word put in the genitive by it; had it been something that governs the genitive, you would very likely see that in poetry, for poetry is what brings licences. What led them to say lawlāka in the position of the nominative is only that they find the pronoun identical in form in the genitive and the accusative — one says ḍarabtuka and marartu bika — and they find it also identical in the nominative, accusative and genitive — one says ḍarabanā and marra binā, so the genitive and accusative are with nā, and then one says qumnā and faʿalnā, so the nominative is with nā. Since that was so, they allowed the kāf to be nominative in the place of anta, since the i'rab of pronouns is by indicators, not by vowels.
The poet said:

أيطمع فينا مَن أراقَ دماءنَا * ولولاكَ لم يعرض لأحسابنا حَسَمْ
(Does he who shed our blood covet us? Were it not for you, Ḥasam would not have assailed our honour.)

And another said:

ومنزلةٍ لولاَىَ طِحْتَ كَمَا هَوَىَ * بأجرامِهِ مِنْ قُلَّة النِّيق مُنْهَوِى
(And many a position where, were it not for me, you would have perished, as one falls with his body from the summit of a peak.)

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ﴾ ("We have sent down the Reminder and We are its guardians"). It is said that the hāʾ in (له) means the Qurʾān; (حَافِظُونَ) means "watching over". It is also said that the hāʾ refers to Muḥammad ﷺ: "and We are guardians of Muḥammad".

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ ("thus We insert it into the hearts of the criminals"). The hāʾ in (نَسْلكه) refers to the denial, i.e. thus We insert the denial. He is saying: ﴿نجعله فى قلوبهم ألاَّ يؤمنوا﴾ ("We place it in their hearts, that they do not believe") [Translator's note: these words are the commentator's paraphrase, though the text encloses them in Quranic brackets].

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِم بَاباً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ فَظَلُّواْ﴾ ("and if We opened to them a gate of heaven and they continued [ascending]"), meaning the angels: they kept ascending through that gate and descending — ﴿لَقَالُوا إنما سُكِّرت أبصارنا﴾ ("they would say: our eyes have only been dazzled"). It is also read ﴿سُكِرَت﴾, and their meanings are close. As for sukkirat, it means "held back": the Arabs say "the wind sakarat" when it has become still and calm. And it is said: "covered over"; covering and holding back (al-ḥays) [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently al-ḥabs] are nearly the same.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾ ("then a clear flaming meteor pursues him"). He is saying: it does not snatch him (lā yakhṭafuhu) [Translator's note: so in the text; probably «لا يخطئه», "it does not miss him"]: it either kills him or deranges him.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَاهَا﴾ ("and the earth We spread out"), i.e. We stretched it, which is spreading. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا﴾ ("and cast therein firm mountains and caused to grow therein"), i.e. in the mountains, ﴿مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ﴾ ("of every well-weighed thing"). He is saying: of gold, silver, lead, copper and iron; that is what is weighed.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشَ﴾ ("and We made for you means of living therein"), meaning the earth, ﴿وَمَن لَّسْتُمْ لَهُ بِرَازِقِينَ﴾ ("and those for whom you are not providers"). Man is in the position of the accusative. He is saying: We made for you therein livelihoods, and male and female slaves.
It has come [in the exegesis] that they are the wild animals and the cattle; but man is not used for cattle alone nor for anything other than people. If it is as was related, we consider that the slaves were included among them, meaning that We gave you possession of slaves, camels, sheep and the like; so that became permissible.
It is also said that (مَن) is in the position of the genitive, meaning: "We made for you therein livelihoods, and for those [for whom you are not providers]". How seldom the Arabs refer a genitive back onto a genitive that has been expressed by a pronoun! Yet the poet said:

تُعلَّق فى مثل السوارى سُيُوفُنا * وما بينها والكَعْبِ غَوْط نفانف
(Our swords are hung on [necks] like masts, and between them and the ankle is a deep chasm.)

He referred "the ankle" back to (بينها). And another said:

هلاَّ سألت بذى الجماجم عنهم * وأبى نُعَيم ذى اللِّواء المُحرْق
(Why did you not ask at Dhū al-Jamājim about them, and about Abū Nuʿaym, he of the burnt banner?)

He referred (أبى نعيم) back to the hāʾ in (عنهم).

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا ٱلرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ﴾ ("and We sent the fertilising winds"). It is also read (الريح) ("the wind"); Ḥamza read it so. Whoever says al-rīḥa lawāqiḥa uses the plural "lawāqiḥ" while "wind" is singular because al-rīḥ has a plural meaning — do you not see that you say "the wind came from every place"? — hence lawāqiḥ was said for that reason; just as it is said: "I left him in a land aghfāl and sabāsib" (al-Farrāʾ said: aghfāl: with no landmark in it), and "mahāriq", and "a garment akhlāq (tattered)". Of it is the saying of the poet:

جاء الشتاءُ وَقميصى أخلاقْ * شراذِمٌ يَضحك مِنه التَّواقْ
(Winter has come and my shirt is in tatters, shreds at which al-Tawwāq laughs.)

As for whoever says (الرياحَ لواقَح), it is clear. But it may be said: the wind is only a fertiliser (mulqiḥa) that fertilises the trees, so how was it said lawāqiḥ ("fertilised")? There are two meanings in that. One of them is that you make the wind itself be what becomes fertilised (talqaḥu), by passing over the earth and the water, so that it carries fertilising matter, and it is said "a wind lāqiḥ", as it is said "a camel lāqiḥ (pregnant)". Evidence for that is that He described the wind of punishment, saying: ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ الريحَ العَقِيم﴾ ("upon them the barren wind"), making it barren since it was not fertilised. The other way is that it is described by fertilisation even though it is what fertilises, as it is said "a sleeping night" while the sleep is in it, and "a concealing secret"; and as it was said:

* الناطق المبروز والمختوم *
(The speaking [document], the publicised and the sealed.)

He made it mabrūz without [a corresponding] verb, i.e. that is one of its attributes; so mafʿūl was permissible in place of mufʿal, just as fāʿil was permissible in place of mafʿūl, since the form was not referred back to the verb.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾ ("We know those of you who go ahead and We know those who lag behind"). That is because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah and His angels send blessings on the first rows in the prayer." So the people rushed to them, and one of the Muslims wanted to sell his distant house in order to come near the mosque and reach the first row. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا المُسْتَقْدِمين مِنْكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمنَا المُسْتَأخِرين﴾: We shall reward them according to their intentions. So the people settled down.

farraa:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿مِن صَلْصَالٍ﴾ ("from sounding clay"). It is said that ṣalṣāl is pure clay mixed with sand, so that it rings (yuṣalṣilu) like pottery. Al-masnūn is "altered" — and Allah knows best — taken from "I rubbed (sanantu) the stone on the stone"; what comes out from between them is called al-sanīn.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿مِن نَّارِ ٱلسَّمُومِ﴾ ("from the fire of scorching wind"). It is said that it is a fire with the veil before it. He said: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from a man, from al-Ḥasan, who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created al-Jānn, the father of the jinn, from the fire of al-samūm, which is a fire with the veil before it. ﴿وهذا الصوت الذى تسمعونه عند الصواعق من انعطاط الحجاب﴾ ("and this sound that you hear at the thunderbolts is from the tearing of the veil") [Translator's note: these words are al-Ḥasan's, not Quranic, though the text encloses them in Quranic brackets].

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿فَقَعُواْ لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ﴾ ("then fall down prostrating to him"): a prostration of greeting and obedience, not of lordship. It is like His saying in Yūsuf: ﴿وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدا﴾ ("and they fell down prostrating to him").

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ﴾ ("except Your sincere servants among them"); it is also read ﴿المُخْلِصِينَ﴾. Whoever puts kasra on the lām makes the action theirs, as in His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وأَخْلَصُوا دِينَهُمْ﴾ ("and they made their religion sincere"); and whoever puts fatḥa [means that] Allah made them sincere (purified them), as in His saying: ﴿إنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ﴾ ("We purified them with a pure quality: remembrance of the abode").

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ ("this is a path [leading] to Me, straight"). He is saying: their return is to Me and I shall requite them. It is like His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّك لَبِالمِرْصَاد﴾ ("your Lord is ever watchful") in al-Fajr. In speech of this kind it is permissible to say to someone you threaten: "Your path is upon me, and I am on your path" — do you not see that He said ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ لبِالمرصَادِ﴾? This is like your saying: "I am on your path". ﴿وصِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ﴾ means: this is a path upon Me, and your path is upon Me. Some read (هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلِىٌّ) ("this is a lofty path"), nominative, making it a naʿt (adjective) of "path", as you say: "a raised, straight path".

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿لَهَا سَبْعَةُ أَبْوَابٍ لِكُلِّ بَابٍ مِّنْهُمْ﴾ ("it has seven gates; for every gate of them"), meaning of the disbelievers, ﴿جُزْءٌ مَّقْسُومٌ﴾ ("is an assigned portion"). He is saying: a known share. The seven gates are levels, one above another: the lowest of them is al-Hāwiya and the highest of them is Jahannam.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿أَبَشَّرْتُمُونِي عَلَىٰ أَن مَّسَّنِيَ ٱلْكِبَرُ﴾ ("do you give me good tidings although old age has touched me?"). Had there been no (على) in it [Translator's note: the text has «لر لم», evidently for «لو لم»], it would also be correct. Similar to it is ﴿حَقِيقٌ عَلَى أَنْ لاَ أَقُولَ﴾ ("obligated not to say"), while in the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (حَقِيقٌ بِأَنْ لاَ أَقُولَ). Similar to it in speech: "I came to you [thinking] that you give, but I did not find you giving", meaning: "I came to you on the basis that you give, and I do not see you so".
His saying: ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾ ("so of what do you give good tidings?"): the nūn has fatḥa, because it is a verb of theirs whose object was not mentioned; that is permissible in speech.
The people of Medina put kasra on it, wanting to make the nūn [the sign of] the object. It is as though they doubled the nūn, saying ﴿فبمَ تُبَشِّرُونِّ قَالُوا﴾, and then lightened it, while the intention is the doubling, as in the saying of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib:

رأته كالثُّغَام يُعَلُّ مِسْكاً * يسوء الفالياتِ إذا فَلَيْنِى
فأُقسم لو جعلتُ عَلىَّ نَذْراً * بطعنةِ فارس لقضَيتُ دَيْنِى
(She saw it [my hair] like white thughām plant, soaked again and again in musk, vexing the women who search it when they search me. I swear, had I made a vow upon myself of a horseman's thrust, I would have paid my debt.)

The Arabs have lightened the nūn of accusative-governing anna and still carried out its accusative government, and that is more drastic than this. The poet said:

فلو أَنْكِ فى يوم الرخاء سألتنِى * فراقَكِ لم أبخل وأنت صديق
فما رُدَّ تزويج عَليه شهادة * وما رُدَّ من بعد الحَرَار عَتِيقُ
(Had you, on a day of ease, asked me to part from you, I would not have withheld it while you were a friend. But no marriage that has been witnessed is revoked, and no freed slave is returned after freedom.)

And another said:

لقد علم الضَّيفُ والمُرْمِلونَ * إذا اغبرَّ أُفْقٌ وهبَّت شَمَالا
بأنْك الربيعُ وغيث مَرِيع * وقدْماً هناك تكون الثِّمَالا
(The guest and the destitute know well, when the horizon turns dusty and the north wind blows, that you are the spring and abundant rain, and that of old you have been there the refuge.)

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ ٱلأَمْرَ أَنَّ دَابِرَ هَؤُلآءِ مَقْطُوعٌ﴾ ("and We conveyed to him that decree: that the last remnant of these would be cut off"). Anna has fatḥa as referred back to "the decree", so it is in the position of the accusative by the decreeing falling upon it. It may also be accusative in another way, by the dropping of the preposition from it, i.e. We decreed that matter with this. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (وَقُلْنَا إنّ دابِرَ) ("and We said: the remnant…"); on this basis, had it been read with kasra it would be a valid way. As for ﴿مُّصْبِحِينَ﴾, it means: when they entered the morning; and mushriqīn: when they entered the sunrise, that is, when the sun rose (sharaqat). Al-dābir: the root. Sharaqat: it rose; ashraqat: it shone.

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِلْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ﴾ ("in that are signs for those who discern"). It is said: for those who reflect; and it is said: for those who look and perceive.

farraa:78-78.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلأَيْكَةِ﴾ ("the thicket"). Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it ﴿ٱلأَيْكَةِ﴾ with hamza throughout the Qurʾān. The people of Medina read it so too, except in al-Shuʿarāʾ and in Ṣād, where they made it without alif and lām and did not decline it [as a diptote]. We consider — and Allah knows best — that in these two places it was written on the basis of dropping the hamza, so the alif fell out because the lām received a vowel. So the reading in them ought to be with alif and lām, because it is one and the same place according to both parties. Al-ayka is a thicket.

farraa:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمَا لَبِإِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾ ("and both were on a clear highway"). He is saying: on a road of theirs which they passed along on their journeys. He made the road an imām because it is headed for (yuʾammu) and followed.

farraa:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتاً آمِنِينَ﴾ ("they carved houses out of the mountains, feeling secure") — [secure] from their falling on them. And it is said: secure from death.

farraa:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾ ("and We have given you seven of the oft-repeated"), meaning the Opening of the Book, which is seven verses according to the people of Medina and the people of al-ʿIrq [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently al-ʿIrāq]. The people of Medina count ﴿أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيهِمْ﴾ as a verse. Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "In the name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful" is a verse of al-Ḥamd. Ḥamza used to count it as a verse. And "We have given you" (القُرآنَ العَظيم) ("the great Qurʾān").

farraa:89-90.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَنَا ٱلنَّذِيرُ ٱلْمُبِينُ﴾ ﴿كَمَآ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى ٱلْمُقْتَسِمِينَ﴾ ("I am the clear warner — as We sent down upon the dividers"). He is saying: I warn you of what was sent down upon the dividers. The dividers (al-muqtasimūn) were men of the people of Mecca whom the people of Mecca posted on its mountain passes in the days of the pilgrimage. They said: "If people ask you about the Prophet ﷺ, say: a soothsayer." And to some of them they said: "Say: a sorcerer"; and to some: "one who separates between two [people]"; and to some: "Say: a madman." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down disgrace upon them, and they died — or five of them — the worst of deaths. They were called the dividers because they divided the roads of Mecca among themselves.

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ جَعَلُواْ ٱلْقُرْآنَ عِضِينَ﴾ ("who made the Qurʾān into parts"). He is saying: they split it up, since they made it sorcery, lies and fables of the ancients. Al-ʿiḍūn in the speech of the Arabs is sorcery itself. And it is said: ʿaḍḍawhu, i.e. they split it up, as a sheep or a slaughtered camel is cut into parts. The singular of al-ʿiḍīn is ʿiḍa; its nominative is ʿiḍūn, and its accusative and genitive ʿiḍīn. Some of the Arabs keep it with yāʾ in every case and decline its nūn, saying: ʿiḍīnuka, and "I passed by ʿiḍīnika", and sinīnika; this is frequent in Asad, Tamīm and ʿĀmir. One of Banū ʿĀmir recited to me:

ذرانىَ من نَجْدٍ فإن سِنِينَه * لِعبن بنا شِيبا وشيَّبْننا مُرْدا
متى نَنج حَبْواً من سنينٍ ملحَّةٍ * نُشمِّر لأُخرى تُنزِلُ الأعصم الفَرْدا
(Leave me out of Najd, for its years have toyed with us as grey-haired men and made us grey as beardless youths. Whenever we escape, crawling, from persistent years [of drought], we gird ourselves for another that brings down the lone white-legged ibex.)

And one of Banū Asad recited:

* مثل المَقَالِى ضُربت قُلينُها *
(Like the stick-players whose short sticks have been struck.)

— from al-qula, which is a children's game. And another of them:

* إلى بُرين الصُفْر المَلْوِيات *
(To the twisted rings of brass.)

The singular of al-burīn is bura. Similar to that are al-thubīn and ʿizīn: in them is permissible what is permissible in al-ʿiḍīn and al-sinīn.
That is permissible only in this defective kind which was of three letters and whose third radical (lām) was dropped. When they pluralised it with nūn, they imagined that it was of the pattern fuʿūl when the wāw came — which is a wāw of plurality — falling in the place of the missing letter; so they imagined that it was the original wāw and that the word was on the pattern fuʿūl. Do you not see that they do not say that with al-ṣāliḥīn, al-muslimīn and the like? Likewise their saying al-thubāt and al-lughāt: sometimes they decline its tāʾ with fatḥa [in the accusative] and kasra, while it is a tāʾ of plurality which ought to have kasra in both accusative and genitive; they imagine that it is a hāʾ [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa] and that the alif before it belongs to the root. One of them recited to me:

إذا ما جَلاَهَا بالأُيَام تحيرت * ثُبَاتاً عليَها ذُلّهَا واكتئابها
(When he drove them out with smoke [to collect honey], they [the bees] were bewildered, in swarms, humiliation and gloom upon them.)

And Abū al-Jarrāḥ said in his speech: "There is no people but we have heard their dialects (lughātahum)" — he said: al-Farrāʾ said: Abū al-Jarrāḥ took back, in his speech, the saying lughātahum. That is not permissible with al-ṣāliḥāt and al-akhawāt, because they are complete words, nothing having been dropped from their singular. As for a word from whose beginning something was dropped, like zina, lida and diya, it is not to be treated by analogy with this, because its loss is from its beginning, not from its lām. So whatever of it is feminine or masculine, treat it like the complete words such as al-ṣāliḥīn and al-ṣāliḥāt: say "I saw your peers (lidātika) and lidīka", and do not say lidīnaka nor lidātaka — unless a poet errs with it, for he sometimes likens one thing to another when it departs from its form; just as some did not decline Abū Sammān, though the nūn belongs to its root, from al-saman (fat), because of its resemblance in form to rayyān and the like.

farraa:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ﴾ ("so proclaim openly what you are commanded"). He did not say "what you are commanded with (bihi)"; He meant — and Allah knows best — "proclaim the command". Had there been in the place of (ما) man, or a mā meaning animals, you would bring in the bāʾ after it, as we say: "Go to whom you are commanded [to go] (bihi)", and "Ride what you are commanded [to ride] (bihi)". But in meaning it stands as a maṣdar (verbal noun); do you not see that you say "How excellent is what you set off (mā tanṭaliqu)!", because you mean "how excellent is your setting off" [Translator's note: the text has «ممَا أحسن», evidently for «ما أحسن»], and "How excellent is what you command when you command!", because you mean "how excellent is your command". Similar to it is His saying: ﴿يَأَبَتِ افْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِى إنْ شَاءَ اللهُ﴾ ("O my father, do what you are commanded; you will find me, if Allah wills…"), as though it was said to him: "do the command which you are commanded". Had a person or something else been meant by it, it would be permissible even if the bāʾ were not made overt, because the Arabs say: "I command you (āmuruka) and I command for you (āmuru bika)", and "akfuruka and akfuru bika (I disbelieve in you)" with one meaning. The like of it is frequent; of it is their saying:

إذا قالت حَذَامِ فأنصتُوها * فإنّ القول ما قالت حذامِ
(When Ḥadhām speaks, listen to her, for the true word is what Ḥadhām says.)

He meant: "listen to her". And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: (أَلاَ إنّ ثَمُودَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ) ("surely Thamūd disbelieved their Lord"), which stands in the place of ﴿يكفرون بالله﴾ ("they disbelieve in Allah") [Translator's note: these words are the commentator's, though the text encloses them in Quranic brackets] and (كفروا بربهم) ("they disbelieved in their Lord"). Iṣdaʿ: make your religion manifest.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «ربما»: a restraining particle and a restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa), having no governing effect. «لو» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar is the object of the wishing. The clause «ربما يود» is resumptive, and the clause «كانوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «يأكلوا» is jussive (majzūm) because it falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. The clause «فسوف يعلمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and «قرية» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إلا» is for restriction. The clause «ولها كتاب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قرية»; the owner of the ḥāl may be indefinite because the indefinite comes after a negation and the clause is joined with the wāw of circumstance.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and «أمة» is the fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «الذي» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and the clause «إنك لمجنون» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «لو ما» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). The clause «إن كنت من الصادقين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ننزل». «إذًا» is a particle of answer, and the clause «وما كانوا» is conjoined to «ما ننزل».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «نحن» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in «إنا»; «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في شيع» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of the implied object, i.e. "We sent messengers among the sects".

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and «رسول» is the fāʿil (agent). The clause «كانوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «يأتيهم».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «كذلك»: the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "We insert it with an inserting like that inserting", and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «نسلكه» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «لا يؤمنون به» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in {نَسْلُكُهُ}, i.e. "not believed in". The clause «وقد خلت سنة الأولين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a qualifier of «بابا», and the clause «يعرجون» is the khabar (predicate) of «ظل», in the position of an accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «لقالوا» is the answer of «لو». «بل»: a particle of digression (iḍrāb), and the clause after it is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «لقد جعلنا» is the answer to the oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun «في السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «إلا من استرق»: a particle of exception; «من» is a relative noun, a connected excepted (mustathnā muttaṣil).

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «والأرض»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الأرض» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «مددنا». The implied clause «مددنا» is conjoined to the clause {جَعَلْنَا} in verse (16), and the clause «مددناها» is explicative; the clause «وألقينا» is conjoined to the implied «مددنا». The preposition and its genitive noun «من كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied naʿt (adjective), i.e. "kinds being of every thing".

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The two prepositional phrases «لكم فيها» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. «ومَن»: a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «معايش». The bāʾ in the khabar (predicate) of «ليس» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «وإن من شيء»: the wāw is resumptive; «إن» is negating, «شيء» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); «إلا» is for restriction. «عندنا» is a ẓarf (adverb) of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ «خزائنه», and the clause «عندنا خزائنه» is the khabar of «شيء».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «لواقح» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الرياح». «فأسقيناكموه»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the kāf and the hāʾ are two objects, the mīm is for the plural, and the wāw is for lengthening (ishbāʿ). The clause «وما أنتم له بخازنين» is a ḥāl from the pronoun of address in «أسقيناكموه», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like «ليس».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «نحن» is a detached pronoun, the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «نحيي» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). [Translator's note: as written; the clause «نحيي» is the khabar of «نحن», and «نحن نحيي» the khabar of «إن», as in the parallel note on 15:25.] The clause «ونحن الوارثون» is conjoined to the clause «نحن نحيي».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المستقدمين».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «هو» is a detached pronoun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «هو يحشرهم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من حمإ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «صلصال».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «والجان»: the wāw is a conjunction; «الجان» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «خَلَقْنا». The two prepositional phrases «من قبل» and «من نار» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلقناه»; two prepositions of the same form may attach to one verb because their meanings differ: the first is for the beginning of the extent in time, and the second is partitive. The implied clause «خلقنا» is conjoined to the clause {خَلَقْنَا} in the previous verse, and the mentioned clause «خَلَقْنا» is explicative of the implied one.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «وإذ»: the wāw is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, the object of an implied «اذكر». «بشرا» is the object of «خالق»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من صلصال» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بشرا», and the preposition and its genitive noun «من حمإ» is attached to a naʿt of «صلصال». The clause «قال» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), in the position of a genitive.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «فإذا»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «إذا» is a conditional adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. "your falling down is required when I have fashioned him". The two prepositional phrases are attached to «نفخت», and the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to «ساجدين». The conditional clause is conjoined to the clause {إِنِّي خَالِقٌ}, and the clause «فقعوا» is the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: «أجمعون»: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the tawkīd «كلهم», nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «أبى» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar is the object of «أبى».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «ما لك»: «ما» is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition and its genitive noun «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the clause «ما لك» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive. The interpreted maṣdar «ألا تكون» is accusative by removal of the preposition (في).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: (لم أكن لأسجد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar made from «أن», which comes after the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and what follows it is genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied khabar (predicate) of «كان», i.e. «مريدا». The preposition and its genitive noun «من حمإ» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «صلصال», and «مسنون» is a naʿt of «حمإ»; the clause «خلقته» is a naʿt of «بشر».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «فاخرج»: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you refuse to prostrate, then go out". The clause «فإنك رجيم» is conjoined to the clause «فاخرج».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «إلى يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اللعنة». The clause «وإن عليك اللعنة» is conjoined to the clause {فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ}, in the position of a jussive.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «فأنْظِرْني»: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if You drive me away, then give me respite"; the implied conditional clause is the answer to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «فإنك»: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want that, then you…".

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «إلى يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {الْمُنْظَرِينَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «بما»: the bāʾ is a preposition of causation; «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُزَين». The object of «أزين» is omitted, i.e. "acts of disobedience". The preposition and its genitive noun «في الأرض» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied object. The clause «ولأغوينهم» is conjoined to the clause «لأزينن», and «أجمعين» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عبادك».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «عليَّ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «صراط», and «مستقيم» is a second naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «ليس»; the preposition and its genitive noun «عليهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سلطان». «من» is a relative, a disconnected excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ), and what is meant by "servants" is the sincere ones, as evidenced by its absence in the verse of al-Isrāʾ: {إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانٌ}. The preposition and its genitive noun «من الغاوين» is attached to a ḥāl from the agent pronoun, i.e. "followed you, being of the deviators".

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «أجمعين»: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «موعدهم».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «لها سبعة أبواب» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ», and the clause «لكل باب منهم جزء» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سبعة»; the link is implied, i.e. "for each gate of them". The preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جزء».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بسلام» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, i.e. "accompanied", and «آمنين» is a second ḥāl. The clause «ادخلوها» is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied saying, i.e. "the angels say to them".

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «نزعنا» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ}. The preposition and its genitive noun «في صدورهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause); the preposition and its genitive noun «من غل» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما». «إخوانا» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «صدورهم»; a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is permitted because the muḍāf is part of the muḍāf ilayhi. The preposition and its genitive noun «على سرر» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «إخوانا», and «متقابلين» is a second naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «لا يمسهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in {مُتَقَابِلِينَ}. The clause «وما هم منها بمخرجين» is conjoined to the clause «لا يمسهم», and the bāʾ in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like «ليس», is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أني أنا الغفور» takes the place of the second and third objects, and the clause «أنا الغفور» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The maṣdar «وأن عذابي ...» is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar, and «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: «إذ» is a ẓarf (adverb) of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the preceding «نبئهم». «سلاما»: stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, and it is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar); the clause «نُسَلِّم سلاما» is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). The preposition and its genitive noun «منكم» is attached to the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The clause «إنا نبشِّرك» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أنْ مَسَّني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first-person pronoun, i.e. "have you given me good news in my state of being touched by old age?". «فبم تبشرون»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive, its alif dropped for lightness; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to «تبشرون», and the clause is conjoined to «بشرتموني».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «فَلا تَكُنْ» is conjoined to the clause «بَشَّرْنَاكَ».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: (قال ومن يقنط) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl) is an implied clause, i.e. "I do not despair". The clause «وَمَنْ يَقْنَطُ» is conjoined to the implied clause. «مَنْ»: an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يقنط» is the khabar (predicate) of the interrogative «مَنْ». «الضَّالون»: a badal (substitute) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يقنط».

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The clause «فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, in the position of a jussive, and the condition with its apodosis is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), i.e. "if you have come for something other than that, then what is your business?". «ما» is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خطبكم» is its khabar (predicate). The clause «أَيُّها المُرْسَلُونَ» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and «والمرسلون» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «إلا آلَ» is accusative (manṣūb) as excepted. The clause «إنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ» is resumptive. «أجمعين»: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «قَدَّرْنَا» is resumptive, and the clause «إنَّهَا لَمنَ الْغَابِرين» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «قَدَّرْنَا», which is made to include the meaning of «عَلِمنا»; the hamza of «إنَّ» takes kasra because of the lām coming in the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «قال» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: (قالوا بل جئناك) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl) is implied, i.e. "we are not ones to be found strange". The clause «بل جِئْنَاكَ» is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يمترون».

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: The clause «وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «أَتَيْنَاكَ».

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: «فَأَسْرِ»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the clause «أتيناك». The preposition and its genitive noun «بِأَهْلِكَ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أسرِ»; the preposition and its genitive noun «بِقِطْعٍ» is attached to «أسرِ»; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنَ الليل» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «قِطْعٍ». The preposition and its genitive noun «منكم» is attached to a ḥāl from «أحد», and the clause «تؤمرون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: «الأمر» is a badal (substitute), and the interpreted maṣdar «أن دابر ...» is a badal from «الأمر».

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The clause «يستبشرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أهل».

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The clause «فلا تفضحون» is conjoined to the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). «تفضحون»: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the implied yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: «أولم ننهك»: the hamza is for interrogation, and the wāw conjoins to an implied element, i.e. "did we not warn you", and the clause «أولم ننهك» is conjoined to the implied content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: «هؤلاء بناتي»: the demonstrative is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied verb, i.e. "marry", and «بناتي» is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative. The implied clause «تزوَّجوا» is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause «إن كنتم فاعلين» is resumptive within the scope of the speech; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: «لعمرك»: the lām is the lām of inception (ibtidāʾ); «عمرك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being «قَسَمي». The preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar, and the clause «يعمهون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in what the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to.

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The clause «فأخذتهم» is resumptive, and «مشرقين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «أخذتهم».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: «جعل» takes two objects: «عاليها سافلها». The preposition and its genitive noun «من سجيل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حجارة».

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «للمتوسِّمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آيات».

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: (وإنها لبسبيل مقيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «للمؤمنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية».

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: (وإن كان أصحاب الأيكة لظالمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive; «إنْ» is lightened from the heavy form and inoperative, and the lām is the one distinguishing the lightened «إن» from the negating one, so it attaches to the lightened one. «ظالمين» is the khabar (predicate) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: The clause «فانتقمنا» is conjoined to the clause «إن كان أصحاب», and the clause «وإنهما لبإمام» is conjoined to the clause «انتقمنا».

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: The clause «وآتيناهم» is conjoined to the clause {كَذَّبَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: «آمنين»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «ينحتون».

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: «مصبحين»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «أخذَتهم».

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: The clause «فما أغنى» is conjoined to the clause «أخذتهم»; «ما» in «ما كانوا» is maṣdar-forming, and the maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of «أغنى».

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun «نا». «الصفح»: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «فاصفح» is conjoined to the clause «إن الساعة لآتية».

harrat-mujtaba:86-86.t: «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). «العليم» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: «والقرآن»: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «سبعا»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من المثاني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «سبعا».

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: «لا تمدَّن»: «لا» is prohibitive; «تمدنَّ» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn of emphasis, in the position of a jussive, and the nūn is for emphasis. The preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «أزواجا».

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: «أنا»: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in «إني». «المبين» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: «كما»: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", a naʿt (adjective) of an implied mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verb that made the omitted object accusative is implied, because the word «النذير» points to it, i.e. "I warn you of a punishment like that which We sent down upon the dividers".

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: «الذين» is not an object of «النذير» in verse (89), because it is qualified by «المبين», and a qualified participle does not govern; so it is a naʿt (adjective) of «المقتسمين». «عضين»: a second object, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is treated like a sound masculine plural.

harrat-mujtaba:92-92.t: The clause «فوربك» is resumptive, and the clause «لنسألنَّهم» is the answer to the oath. «أجمعين»: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «نسألهم».

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «عمَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نسألنهم».

harrat-mujtaba:94-94.t: (بما تؤمر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the genitive maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:96-96.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «فسوف يعلمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:97-97.t: (أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar takes the place of the two objects of «نعلم»; «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the genitive maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضيق».

harrat-mujtaba:98-98.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «سبح».

harrat-mujtaba:99-99.t: The clause «واعبد» is conjoined to the clause «كن».

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {كَذَلِك نسلكه}: the kāf is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). The hāʾ in نسلكه refers to the denial; it has also been said, to the Reminder (الذكر).

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {فظلوا فِيهِ يعرجون}: the pronoun in فظلوا and in يعرجون is for the angels, i.e. if Allah opened a gate in the heaven and the angels ascended through it while the disbelievers were watching, they would say: "Our eyes have only been dazzled (سكرت), and we have been bewitched". The meaning of سكرت is "covered", i.e. veiled. It has also been said the pronoun is for the disbelievers, i.e. if Allah opened a gate in the heaven and they themselves ascended through it, they would not believe, and would say: "We have been bewitched and our eyes have been dazzled". The hāʾ in فيه is for the gate.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {إِلَّا من اسْترق السّمع}: من is in the position of accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Al-Zajjāj permitted من to be in the position of genitive, on the implied form "except from whoever steals a hearing (إِلَّا مِمَّن اسْترق السّمع)", and this is far-fetched.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted, {رُبمَا}: there are four dialectal forms of it: one says رُبَمَا, lightened, and رُبَّمَا, doubled, and رُبَتَمَا with tāʾ and lightening, and with tāʾ and doubling, by making the word feminine. Abū Ḥātim related the four forms with fatḥa on the rāʾ. It has no grammatical position. مَا was brought to restrain رُبّ from governing; it has also been said it was brought to make possible the occurrence of a verb after it. Al-Akhfash said مَا is in the position of genitive by رُبّ, and it is indefinite.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {وَمن لَسْتُم لَهُ برازقين}: من is in the position of accusative by conjunction to the position of لكم, because the meaning of جعلنَا لكم فِي الأَرْض معايش is "We sustained you and strengthened you, and those for whom you are not providers". It is also permissible to put من in the accusative on the implication of a verb, its implied form being "and We made for you livelihoods in the earth, and We sustained those for whom you are not providers". Al-Farrāʾ permitted من to be in the position of genitive by conjunction to the kāf and mīm in لكم; conjoining to a genitive [pronoun without repeating the preposition] is not permissible according to the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ also permitted من to be in the position of accusative by conjunction to معايش, on the basis that من means the slave-women and slaves, i.e. We made for you in the earth what you eat, and We made for you those who serve you and whom you enjoy.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّيَاح لَوَاقِح}: the original of the expression was ملاقح, because it is from ألقحت الرّيح الشّجر ("the wind fertilized the trees"), so it is ملقح, plural ملاقح; but it came on the assumption of dropping the augment, as though it came from لقحت, so it is لاقح, plural لواقح. So the wording came on this assumption while the meaning is on the other, because it is only transitive with the augment. Ḥamza read الرّيح لواقح in the singular, and Abū Ḥātim rejected it because of the singular wording of الريح with the plural attribute; but it is good, because the singular comes with the meaning of the plural: Allah, exalted be His mention, said وَالْملك على أرجائها, meaning the angels; and al-Farrāʾ related "the wind came from every place (جَاءَت الرّيح من كل مَكَان)" — so he said.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {ذرهم}: its pattern is "افعلهم" [Translator's note: so in the text; with the first radical dropped the pattern is properly عَلْهم], and its origin is اوذرهم. The wāw was dropped because it originally fell between a yāʾ and a kasra; it has also been said, between two kasras originally, because the connecting alif has kasra, and the dhāl, even though it has fatḥa in the imperfect, is due kasra, because the past is وذر, and yafʿal with fatḥa does not come from faʿala unless it contains a guttural letter, and there is no guttural letter in وذر. The dhāl was given fatḥa only because it is construed on what has its meaning, namely يدع: since يذر means يدع, and يدع received its fatḥa from the guttural letter while its dāl originally had kasra, the wāw was dropped from يدع according to its origin, and no regard was paid to the fatḥa that the guttural letter produced. Since يذر means يدع and is construed on it in the fatḥa of its middle radical, the wāw was likewise dropped according to the origin — had it been used. When the wāw was dropped for the reason we mentioned, the connecting alif was no longer needed, so ذرهم remained as it is in the recitation; its origin and its cause are what we have mentioned.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {كلهم أَجْمَعُونَ}: أجمعون is a definite word of tawkīd (emphasis), but it does not stand alone as كلهم stands alone: you say كل الْقَوْم أَتَانِي ("all the people came to me"), and you do not say أجمع الْقَوْم أَتَانِي. Al-Mubarrad said أجمعون means "not dispersed"; in the view of others this is an error on his part, because it would oblige him to make it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {إِلَّا إِبْلِيس}: an exception not from [the genus of] the first, according to whoever holds that Iblīs is not of the angels, by His saying كَانَ من الْجِنّ. It has also been said it is an exception from the first, by His saying وَإِذ قُلْنَا للْمَلَائكَة اسجدوا لأدم فسجدوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيس: had he been other than the angels, he would not have been commanded, because the command to prostrate was directed specifically at the angels. The name jinn may apply to the angels because they are concealed from the eyes of the children of Adam; Allah the Exalted said وَلَقَد علمت الْجنَّة إِنَّهُم لمحضرون, and the jinna there are the angels.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying {إِلَّا وَلها كتاب مَعْلُوم}: كتاب is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and لها is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of القرية. Dropping the wāw from ولها would be permissible were it [so] in speech.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying {وَإِن جَهَنَّم}: جهنم is a diptote because it is a definite foreign noun. It has also been said it is Arabic, but it is feminine and definite. Whoever makes it Arabic derives it from their saying ركية جهنام ("a well of great depth"), when it is deep-bottomed; so the Fire was called جهنم because of the depth of its bottom.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {إخْوَانًا على سرر مُتَقَابلين}: إخوانا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المتقين, or from the nominative pronoun in ادخلوها, or from the pronoun in آمنين. It may also be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from the hāʾ and mīm in صدورهم.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t:
His saying {تبشرون}: its origin is تبشرونني, but Nāfiʿ dropped the second nūn, which entered to separate the verb from the yāʾ, because of the meeting of two identical letters, and gave kasra to the nūn that is the sign of the nominative because of its adjacency to the yāʾ, and dropped the yāʾ because the kasra indicates it. This is far-fetched, because of the kasra on the inflectional nūn, whose due is fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and because he brought the sign of the accusative [pronoun] with a yāʾ like the genitive. Kasra on the nūn of the nominative and dropping the nūn that accompanies the yāʾ in the accusative pronoun has occurred in poetry; al-Aʿshā said:
... أبالموت الَّذِي لَا بُد أَنِّي ... ملاق لَا أَبَاك تخوفيني ...
(Is it with death — which I must inevitably meet — that you frighten me, may you have no father?)
He meant تخوفينني, so he dropped the second nūn and gave kasra to the nūn of the feminine because of its adjacency to the yāʾ; the nūn in تخوفينني is the sign of the nominative in the verb of the singular [feminine], like the nūn in تبشرون, which is the mark of the nominative. Some said the dropped nūn is the first one; that is far-fetched, because it is the mark of the nominative, and the mark of the nominative is not dropped from verbs except because of a jussive or accusative governor.
The body of the readers differed from Nāfiʿ in his reading: Ibn Kathīr read تبشرونّ with the nūn doubled and with kasra; it is a good reading, because he assimilated the nūn that is the mark of the nominative into the nūn that entered to separate the yāʾ from the verb, and dropped the yāʾ because the kasra indicates it. The body of the readers other than these two read with a lightened nūn with fatḥa, which is the mark of the nominative, and did not make the verb pass to an object as Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr did.
