nahhas-irab:80-80.t: It was said: the companions of al-Ḥijr are the people of Ṣāliḥ.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: Al-Ḥasan read وَكانُوا يَنْحِتُونَ because it contains one of the guttural letters; and the kasra is more eloquent. «[Translator's note: so printed, with kasra; the explanation (a guttural letter) and the remark that kasra is more eloquent imply that al-Ḥasan's reading is meant with fatḥa (يَنْحَتُونَ).]»

nahhas-irab:87-88.t: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْناكَ سَبْعاً مِنَ الْمَثانِي وَالْقُرْآنَ الْعَظِيمَ: in the hadith, the Quran here is al-Ḥamd [i.e. al-Fātiḥa], because part of the Quran is Quran. لا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أَزْواجاً مِنْهُمْ: do not covet their blessings, and do not grieve over them, i.e. over My blessing upon them. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of وَاخْفِضْ جَناحَكَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ is: soften your wing towards whoever believes in you and follows you.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: The original of إِنَّا is (إنّنا). نَحْنُ is in the position of an accusative as an emphasis (tawkīd) of [the pronoun governed by] (إنّ); it is permissible for it to be in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is permissible for it to have no position, being a separating pronoun (fāṣila). وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ: the first lām is a genitive-governing lām and the second is a lām of emphasis; no differentiation was needed with the pronoun because the marking differs.

nahhas-irab:90-91.t: كَما أَنْزَلْنا: the kāf is in the position of an accusative, i.e. «And say: I am indeed the clear warner» of a punishment or chastisement like what We sent down upon the dividers. الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا الْقُرْآنَ عِضِينَ: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā holds that «عضين» is from عضّيت, i.e. I divided, and it is derived from (العضو) "limb"; what is omitted according to him is a wāw, and the diminutive according to him is (عضيّة). Al-Kisāʾī holds that it is from عضهت الرجل, i.e. I accused the man falsely, and the diminutive according to him is (عضيهة). Al-Farrāʾ said: (العضون) in the speech of the Arabs is sorcery. According to the Basrans it is pluralized with wāw and nūn only as compensation for what was dropped from it; and according to the Kufans it ought to have been pluralized on the pattern (فعول), so they sought the wāw that is in (فعول) and brought it, saying (عضون). Al-Farrāʾ said: some of the Arabs say عضينك, making it with yāʾ in every case and inflecting the nūn, as you say مضت سنينك ("your years have passed"); this is common among Asad, Tamīm and ʿĀmir. The reason for it according to him is that since the wāw occurred in the place of a defective letter, they imagined it was the wāw of (فعول), so they inflected what follows it and changed it into a yāʾ, just as some Arabs said with the tāʾ — he related it from Abū al-Jarrāḥ: سمعت لغاتهم ("I heard their dialects", with the tāʾ inflected). But you do not say that with (الصّالحات), nor with what has had its beginning dropped, such as (لدّات).

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: An emphasis (tawkīd) of the hāʾ and mīm.

nahhas-irab:94-94.t:
Abū Isḥāq said: فَاصْدَعْ بِما تُؤْمَرُ, i.e. make it plain and manifest it; derived from (الصّديع), which is the dawn; and a crack (الصّدع) in glass is when parts of it separate from one another. بِما تُؤْمَرُ: [ما with the verb] is a maṣdar according to the Basrans, i.e. "with Our command". Al-Kisāʾī said: the implied structure is "with what you are commanded with (به)", like أَلا إِنَّ عاداً كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ [Hūd: 60], i.e. "in their Lord", and then the bāʾ was dropped. «[Translator's note: the source prints «هود: 6»; the verse is Hūd 60.]» Abū Jaʿfar said: dropping the bāʾ is not permissible according to the Basrans, neither in prose nor in poetry. The Kufans recited, by Jarīr: [wāfir] 262-
تمرّون الدّيار ولم تعوجوا ... كلامكم عليّ إذا حرام
(You pass the abodes and do not turn aside; speaking to you is then forbidden to me.)
And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I heard ʿUmāra ibn ʿAqīl ibn Bilāl ibn Jarīr recite it for his grandfather as:
مررتم بالدّيار ولم تعوجوا
(You passed by the abodes and did not turn aside.)

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: الَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ: in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (المستهزئين). And the meaning of وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ [al-Ḥijr: 94] is: from answering them when they meet you with ugliness.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: حَتَّى يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ: [يَأْتِيَكَ is] accusative by (حتّى), and its nominative is not permissible because it is future. (اليقين) is death, because every rational person is certain of it.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِي شِيَعِ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
That is, the sects of the ancients.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَِ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ḥumayd, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: Thus We insert the shirk. [Translator's note: so printed («الحسين»); al-Ḥasan (al-Baṣrī) is probably meant.]
Abū ʿUbayd said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us from Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»], from Mujāhid, who said: We insert the giving of the lie.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view held by the exegetes and the people of language, except those who deviate among them; for some of them said: the meaning is "thus We insert the Qurʾān." They argued that when the Prophet ﷺ recited the Qurʾān to them and made them hear it and it reached their hearts — and that was by Allah's command and power — it was Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, who inserted it into their hearts in this sense.
And it was said: since He created them with a constitution by which they understand the revelation that comes to them — when He created them with a constitution by which they understand what inserts that into their hearts, it is as though He inserted it.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتْ سُنَّةُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾.
That is, their way has gone before in giving the lie to the signs and proofs, and in their unbelief; and these are following in their footsteps.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِم بَاباً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ فَظَلُّواْ فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, and the angels kept ascending through it,
i.e. going and coming.
The people of language said: عَرَجَ يَعْرُجُ when he ascends and rises; and from it is the common people's saying: "So-and-so's soul was taken up (ʿurija)."

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿لَقَالُواْ إِنَّمَا سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصَارُنَا﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: (Our eyes) have been seized.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known of the reading of Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan is (سُكِرَتْ) without shadda.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, bewitched.
Abū ʿUbayd related from Abū ʿUbayda that one says سُكِرتْ أبصارهم when a dimness (samādīr) covers them so that they do not see.
Al-Farrāʾ said: Whoever read (سَكِرِتْ) took it from the stillness of the wind. [Translator's note: the vowelling «سَكِرِتْ» is as printed.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are close to one another, and their root is what Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is from intoxication (al-sukr) from drink.
This is a good view: i.e. something covered them that veiled their sight, as something covers the drunkard that veils his mind.
And sukūr of the wind is its stillness and abating, and that goes back to the meaning of al-takhyīr. [Translator's note: so printed («التخيير»); perhaps «التحيير», "bewilderment," is meant.]

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاءِ بُرُوجاً وَزَيَّنَّاهَا لِلنَّاظِرِينََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Meaning the stars.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And whoever said that they are the twelve zodiacal signs (burūj), his view goes back to this, because they are great stars.
It is well known in the language that one says بَرَج يَبْرُجُ when something appears and rises; so these stars were called burūj because of their visibility, their fixedness and their height. And al-barajj is largeness of the eye.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَّجِيمٍٍ﴾.
That is, he does not reach it, nor hear anything of the revelation except by stealth. This was one of the signs of the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ: we know of no poet who compared anything to the speed of the (shooting) stars except in Islam; had this existed before it, they would have used it as a comparison. [Translator's note: the source has «قله», evidently for «قبله», "before it".]
Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] said: al-rajīm is the accursed.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Every rajīm in the Qurʾān means "the reviled."
And it was said: rajīm means marjūm ("stoned"), i.e. he is pelted with the stars.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍٍ﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ﴾.
He said: That is, known.
Likewise ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated it from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
Abū Ṣāliḥ and ʿIkrima said: That is, measured out.
Mujāhid said: That is, determined by a measure.
Its meaning is: determined, not exceeding Allah's measure nor falling short of it, so it is as though it were weighed.
And it was said: by mawzūn He means what is weighed, of gold, silver, iron, lead and the like.
On this basis the meaning is: and We caused to grow in the mountains of every weighed thing.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوْ كَانُواْ مُسْلِمِينَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Khuṣayf, from Mujāhid, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "A group of the monotheists will enter the Fire, and the polytheists will say to them: What use was your Islam and your faith to you, when you are with us in the Fire? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will bring them out of it, and at that point ﴿يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَروُا لَوْ كَانُوا مُسْلِمِين﴾."
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: That is on the Day of Resurrection.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: (The polytheists will say to those of the monotheists who were made to enter the Fire: What you were upon has not benefited you, and you are in the Fire! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will be angered on their behalf, and they will be brought out to a river called "the River of Life," and they will grow (anew) in it. Then a mark will remain on their faces by which they are known; it will be said: These are "the Jahannamīs." They will ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, to remove that from them, and He will remove it from them and admit them to Paradise. Then the polytheists will wish that they had been Muslims.)
And it was said: When the polytheists see (the truth) with their own eyes, they will wish for Islam.
As for the meaning of (رُبَّ) here: in the speech of the Arabs it is for diminution (taqlīl), and it carries a sense of threat. The Arabs use this a great deal for one whom they threaten and menace [Translator's note: the source has «تتخدّده», evidently for «تتهدّده», "menace"]. A man says to another: "Perhaps you will regret what you are doing" [and they are doubtful of his regretting and do not intend to make it little]; rather, the real meaning is that he is saying: even if it were something that happens rarely, or only once, you ought not to do it.
As for the statement of whoever said that «رُبَّ» is used for multiplicity (taktīr), it is not known in the speech of the Arabs.
And it was said: This will only be on the Day of Resurrection, when they recover from the terrors they are in, so it will be only in some of the stations.
The first view is the soundest.
The proof that it is a warning and a threat is His saying after it: ﴿ذَرْهُمْ يَأْكُلُوا وَيَتَمَتَّعُوا وَيُلْهِهِمُ الأَمَلُ، فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُون﴾.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشََ﴾.
That is, in the earth.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَن لَّسْتُمْ لَهُ بِرَازِقِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Meaning the beasts and the livestock.
Others said: Meaning the slaves and the beasts.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is more fitting, because (مَنْ) is not used for what lacks reason unless beings with reason are mixed in with it.
The meaning is: and We made for you the slaves, the beasts and the livestock.
And it is possible that the meaning is: We gave you a livelihood, and gave a livelihood to those for whom you are not providers.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ عِندَنَا خَزَائِنُهُ﴾.
He informed that the treasuries of things are in His hand,
i.e. that He, Mighty and Majestic is He, is their keeper and the One in charge of managing them.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا ٱلرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The wind carries the water and fertilises the clouds and milks them, so they flow as the milch-camel (al-laqḥa) gives milk; then it rains.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The winds fertilise the trees and the clouds, and milk them.
Abū Rajāʾ said: I said to al-Ḥasan: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا ٱلرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ﴾. He said: They fertilise the trees. I said: And the clouds? He said: And the clouds.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿لَوَاقِح﴾ means malāqiḥ; he holds that it is the plural of mulqiḥa and mulqiḥ, with the augment letters then dropped from it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is far-fetched; dropping augment letters from the like of this is permissible only in poetry. Rather, it is the plural of lāqiḥa.
And «لاَقِحٌ» is literal, without any omission, and it has one of two senses: it may be called lāqiḥ by way of attribution (ʿalā l-nasab), i.e. possessing fertilisation, as though it fertilises the clouds and the trees, as came in the exegesis — and this is the view of Abū ʿAmr.
And it may be called lāqiḥ meaning "pregnant/bearing." The Arabs call the south wind lāqiḥ and ḥāmil ("bearing"), and the north wind ḥāʾil ("barren") and ʿaqīm ("sterile"). And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿حَتَّى إذَا أَقَلَّتْ سَحَابَاً ثِقَالاً﴾ — and «أقلَّت» and «حَمَلَت» ("carried") are one.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿المستقدِمُونَ﴾ are the first generations, and ﴿المستأخِروُن﴾ are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ.
And Sufyān narrated from his father, from ʿIkrima, who said: ﴿المستقْدِمون﴾ are all who have come forth (into existence), and ﴿المستأخِروُن﴾ are all who were in the loins of men.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: ﴿المستقدِمُون﴾ are those who have died, and ﴿المستأخِروُنَ﴾ are the living.
And Sufyān narrated from Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, from Abū l-Jawzāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ﴾ — the first row; ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾ — the last row.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying: Nūḥ ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Mālik narrated to us from Abū l-Jawzāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾ — he said: A beautiful woman used to pray with the Prophet ﷺ. Some men would move forward so as not to see her, and some men would move back, and when the Prophet ﷺ bowed, one of them would put his hand on his knee and look at her from under his upper arm. So Allah sent down ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْنَا ٱلْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ مِن صَلْصَالٍٍ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them was narrated by Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-ṣalṣāl is dry clay.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: It is clay that dries and comes to have a clinking sound (ṣalṣala).
The other view was narrated by Ibn Abī Najīḥ and Ibn Jurayj from Mujāhid, who said: al-ṣalṣāl is the stinking. [Translator's note: the source has «ابن نجيح» and «ابن جريح».]
Abū Jaʿfar said: Both views are possible, though the first is clearer, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالفَخَّارِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda related that dry clay is called ṣalṣāl so long as fire has not touched it; once fire has touched it, it is fakhkhār (pottery).
The people of language recited:
* "كَعَدْوِ المُصَلْصِلِ الجَوَّالِ" *
(Like the running of the roaming, clattering one.)
And al-ṣalṣala is sound.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is pure clay mixed with sand, so a clinking is heard from it.
As for the second view: its origin is ṣilāl, then one of the two lāms was replaced by a ṣād.
[And al-Kisāʾī related that one says صلَّ اللحمُ and أصلَّ when meat goes rotten.]
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ﴾.
[al-ḥamaʾ and al-ḥamaʾa are] black, altered [clay].
There are four views on al-masnūn:
Sufyān narrated from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-masnūn is the stinking.
Likewise Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Man was created from ṣalṣāl, from sticky clay (ṭīn lāzib), which is the good, and from ḥamaʾ masnūn, which is the stinking.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: It is the stinking.
Of the people of language, al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī held this view. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī claimed that the saying of Allah ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾ is from this, and that its origin is (لَمْ يَتَسَنَّنْ), with one of the two nūns replaced by a hāʾ. So this is one view.
The other view — the position of Abū ʿUbayda — is that al-masnūn is "the poured."
And Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-masnūn is the moist.
This is in the sense of "the poured," because it can only be poured when it is moist. This is a good view, because one says سَننْتُ الشَّيءَ, i.e. "I poured it," and in the ḥadīth: "al-Ḥasan used to pour (yasunnu) water over his face"; and if this were from أَسِنَ الماءُ ("the water became stagnant"), it would be muʾsin.
The third view is that of al-Farrāʾ: it is "the rubbed/smoothed," and it can only be altered, from سننْتُ الحديدَ ("I whetted the iron").
The fourth view: it is what is poured into a mould and a form, from sunnat al-wajh (the contour of the face).

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ﴾.
That is, a term which it neither precedes nor goes beyond.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا بِٱلْمَلائِكَةِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾.
The meaning of (لَوْ مَا), (لَوْلاَ) and (هَلاَّ) — "why not?" — is one. The people of language recited:
تعدُّونَ عَقْر النِّيبِ أفضلَ مجدِكُمْ * بَنِي ضَوْطَرَى لَوْلاَ الكَمِيَّ المُقَنَّعَا
(You count the hamstringing of old she-camels as your finest glory, O sons of Ḍawṭarā — why not the helmeted, fully armed warrior?)
i.e. why do you not count the helmeted, fully armed warrior?
And Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»], who said: In this there is fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr).
He holds that its answer is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَوْ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ بَابَاً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَظَلُّوا فِيهِ يَعْرُجُون﴾; he holds that this is connected with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿لَّوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا بِٱلْمَلائِكَةِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿مَا نُنَزِّلُ ٱلْمَلائِكَةَ إِلاَّ بِٱلحَقِّ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, with the message and the punishment.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ إِذاً مُّنظَرِينَ﴾.
That is, if the angels came down, they would not be given respite, nor would their repentance be accepted, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنَا مَلَكَاً لَقُضِيَ الأَمْرُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ﴾.
Thābit and Qatāda said: Allah has guarded it from the devils adding falsehood to it or removing truth from it.
Mujāhid said: It is with Us.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ، إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْمَعْلُومِ﴾.
Sufyān said: It has reached me that the known time is the first blowing (of the Trumpet).

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ [verse 41].
One of the two (views) — and it is the position of Mujāhid — he said: The truth: its path is upon Me, and it comes back to Me; as is said by way of threat: "Your path is upon me (i.e. leads past me), so do what you will," and as the Exalted said: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ﴾. [Translator's note: the source begins «أحدهما» ("one of the two") without first announcing two views.]
The other view: This is a path according to My command and under My will.
And Qays ibn ʿUbāda read ﴿قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ and said: i.e. lofty; its meaning is lofty in religion and truth. [Translator's note: the reading is printed identically to the muṣḥaf; the gloss "lofty" implies the reading «عَلِيٌّ».]

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَاوِينَ﴾ [verse 42].
That is, the astray.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمَوْعِدُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ، لَهَا سَبْعَةُ أَبْوَابٍ لِكُلِّ بَابٍ مِّنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَّقْسُومٌ ٌ﴾.
That is, each of them has a station in the torment according to the degree of his station in sin.
And Mālik ibn Mighwal narrated from Ḥumayd, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hell has seven gates; one gate of them is for whoever draws his sword against my community" — or he said: "against the community of Muḥammad."

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَاناً عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ﴾.
Al-ghill according to the people of language is rancour, resentment and enmity; from it one says غَلَّ يَغِلُّ.
And from al-ghulūl — which is stealing from the spoils — one says غَلَّ يَغُلُّ; and from treachery one says أَغَلَّ يُغِلُّ, as the poet said: [Translator's note: the source has «ويُغال», evidently for «ويُقال», "one says".]
جَزَى اللَّهُ عَنَّا جَمْرَة ابنةَ نَوْفَلٍ * جَزَاءَ مُغِلٍّ بالأَمانةِ كَاذِب
(May Allah repay Jamra daughter of Nawfal on our behalf with the repayment of one treacherous with a trust, a liar.)
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِخْوَاناً عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿مُتَقَابِلِينَ﴾ — he said: None of them looks at the back of his companion's head.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيهَا نَصَبٌٌ﴾.
That is, fatigue.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَبِّىءْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾.
That is, inform.
And it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ came out to his Companions while they were laughing, and said: Do you laugh while Paradise and the Fire are before you? That weighed heavily on them, so Allah sent down ﴿نَبِّىءْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ لاَ تَوْجَلْ﴾.
Its meaning is: do not be alarmed. And al-qāniṭūn are the despairing.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱمْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْنَآ إِنَّهَا لَمِنَ ٱلْغَابِرِينَ﴾.
It was said: «قَدَرْنَا» means "We knew"; and «قدَّرنا» is in its proper sense, i.e. it is in Our decree and in what We informed him of, thus.
Al-ghābir is the one who remains, and it may be used for the one who departs. The meaning is: she is among those who remain behind in the destruction. The people of language recited:
لا تَكْسَعِ الشَّوْلَ بِأَغْبَارِهَا * إنَّكَ لا تَدْرِي مَنَ النَّاتِجُ
(Do not leave the dry she-camels with the remnants of their milk unmilked; you do not know who will deliver their young.)
Al-aghbār are the remnants of milk.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Lūṭ ﷺ did not recognise them.
And it was said: Ibrāhīm ﷺ found them strange, because they did not eat of his food; and they used to regard a guest as suspect if he did not eat.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ بَلْ جِئْنَاكَ بِمَا كَانُواْ فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: With the punishment.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: rather, we have come to you with what they used to doubt — the descent of the punishment upon them.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾.
Al-surā (night travel) is only by night; but His saying, the Exalted, ﴿بِقِطَعٍ﴾ indicates that much of the night has passed.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ﴾.
It was said: He forbade turning to look at what was in the dwellings, lest they be distracted by it from going on.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَضَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ ٱلأَمْرَ﴾.
That is, We informed him of it; then He explained it, saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَنَّ دَابِرَ هَؤُلآءِ مَقْطُوعٌ مُّصْبِحِينَ﴾.
That is, the last of them would be uprooted.
Al-Farrāʾ said: al-dābir is the root.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قَالُواْ أَوَلَمْ نَنْهَكَ عَنِ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
It is narrated that they had forbidden him to host anyone as a guest.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ هَؤُلآءِ بَنَاتِي إِن كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ﴾.
This answer is construed according to the sense. The meaning is: they wanted them (the guests) for depravity, so Lūṭ ﷺ said to them: These are my daughters, so marry.
The best of what has been said on this is that the wives of every prophet are in the position of mothers of his community, and the children of his community are in the position of his children.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونََ﴾.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿لَعَمْرُكَ﴾ — by your life (laʿayshuka).
And Abū l-Jawzāʾ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: By your life (laḥayātuka).
And it is narrated that Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī disliked that a man should say laʿamrī; he said: because its meaning is "by my life."
And so it is according to the people of language.
Sībawayh said: al-ʿamr and al-ʿumr are one, and in oaths they use only the fatḥa, because of its lightness; and laʿumurī has been related; all of it means al-ʿumr (life).
This is a distinction for the Prophet ﷺ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, swore by his life.
Abū l-Jawzāʾ said: I have not heard of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, swearing by the life of anyone other than him ﷺ.
Sufyān said: I asked al-Aʿmash about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾.
He said: He swore by the Prophet that they are wandering to and fro in their heedlessness.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ مُشْرِقِينََ﴾.
That is, the Cry seized them with the punishment at the time of sunrise.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِلْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, for those who discern by signs (al-mutafarrisīn).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, for those who look.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its real sense is: توسَّمتُ الشيءَ — I looked at the thing with the look of one who verifies, until the reality of the thing's mark (sima) became established.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّهَا لَبِسَبِيلٍ مُّقِيمٍ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is "and the signs (are…)," and it is possible that the meaning is "and the city of the people of Lūṭ (is…)."
Mujāhid said: ﴿لَبِسَبِيلٍ مُّقِيمٍ﴾ — on a marked road, i.e. a clear one.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلأَيْكَةِ لَظَالِمِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-ayka is the thicket full of trees.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so it is in the language: a tree is called ayka, and its plural is ayk.
And it is narrated that their trees were dawm (doum palms).
As for the narration of whoever narrated that «لَيْكَةَ» is the name of the town in which they were, and (الأيكةُ) is the whole country, it is not known in the language and is not sound.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمَا لَبِإِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, on a clear road, i.e. they pass by them on their journeys.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the language that a road is called imām, because it is followed and taken as a guide.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أَصْحَابُ ٱلحِجْرِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: al-Ḥijr is the valley; he holds that it is its name.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانُواْ يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتاً آمِنِينَ﴾.
That is, secure (in the belief) that they would not fall down.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱصْفَحِ ٱلصَّفْحَ ٱلْجَمِيلََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: This was before he was commanded to fight.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾.
ʿAbd Khayr narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he said regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾: meaning the Opening of the Book (al-Fātiḥa).
Likewise Abū Hurayra said: It is the Opening of the Book, and «In the name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful» is not part of it.
Likewise Abū Yaḥyā narrated from Mujāhid, and likewise Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda.
And Sufyān ibn Manṣūr narrated from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾. [Translator's note: so printed («سفيان بن منصور»); probably "Sufyān, from Manṣūr".]
He said: The seven long ones (al-sabʿ al-ṭuwal).
Likewise Shuʿba narrated from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي﴾.
He said: The seven long ones: "al-Baqara, Āl ʿImrān, al-Nisāʾ, al-Māʾida, al-Anʿām, al-Aʿrāf and Yūnus."
So it is in the ḥadīth; and likewise al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: They are the seven long ones. And likewise Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: "The seven oft-repeated (al-sabʿ al-mathānī) and the Mighty Qurʾān: the Mother of the Qurʾān."
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿ٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ﴾ — the rest of it.
And it is authentically reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he said: The seven mathānī are al-Ḥamd (al-Fātiḥa); and Qatāda held this.
He explained its meaning, saying: because the Opening of the Book is repeated (tuthannā) in every rakʿa, obligatory or supererogatory.
The meaning on this view is: and We have given you seven verses of what is repeated in the prayer.
And (مِنْ) here, on this view, is for explaining the genus (li-bayān al-jins), as the Exalted said: ﴿فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْس مِنَ الأوْثَانِ﴾.
And it is possible that the meaning is: of that by which Allah is praised (yuthnā), because in al-Ḥamd there is praise (thanāʾ) of Allah, mention of His oneness and of His sovereignty over the Day of Judgement; and on this view (مِنْ) is also for explaining the genus.
And it is possible that it is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), the meaning being: and We have given you seven verses of the mathānī, i.e. of the Qurʾān, in which the verses and stories are repeated and in which Allah is praised.
This is better, and it is the position of Abū Mālik, because he said: ﴿المثاني﴾ is the Qurʾān.
As for those who said they are the seven long ones, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explained his position, saying: because the legal limits and the obligations are repeated in them; so (من) on this view is for explaining the genus.
And it is possible that it is partitive, as preceded.
And Abū ʿUbayd narrated that Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna used to recite this verse, interpreting it in light of the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ: "He is not of us who does not yataghanna with the Qurʾān" — he said: i.e. make himself free of need through it (yastaghnī).
He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded the Prophet ﷺ to be free of need of wealth through the Qurʾān, and the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعاً مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِي وَٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّنْهُمْ﴾.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that he said: "Whoever has memorised the Qurʾān and then considers that anyone has been given something better than what he was given has belittled something great [and magnified something small]."
Mujāhid said regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لاَ تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّنْهُمْ﴾:
He said: The rich, the ones alike, i.e. likes of one another in blessings.
And al-azwāj in the language are the kinds.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلْ إِنِّيۤ أَنَا ٱلنَّذِيرُ ٱلْمُبِينُ. كَمَآ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى ٱلْمُقْتَسِمِينَ﴾.
There is an omission in the statement, and the meaning is: and say, I am the clear warner (of) a punishment like that which We sent down upon al-muqtasimīn.
There are several views about al-muqtasimīn:
One of them: they were a group who swore an alliance to slander (ʿaḍh) the Prophet ﷺ.
The other view: al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿كَمَآ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى ٱلْمُقْتَسِمِينَ﴾, that he said: the Jews and the Christians; ﴿الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا القُرْآنَ عِضِين﴾ — he said: they believed in part of it and disbelieved in part of it.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿المقتسمين﴾ are the People of the Book; they tore the scriptures apart and rejoiced in what they had of them.
Mujāhid said: ﴿المقتسمين﴾ are the people of the (various) religions.
Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] said, and ʿAṭāʾ said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh; they tore apart what they said about the Qurʾān: some of them said it is poetry, some said it is sorcery, and some said it is tales of the ancients; and that is the ʿiḍūn.
ʿIkrima said: ﴿عِضِين﴾ is sorcery.
Abū ʿUbayda held that ﴿عِضِينَ﴾ is taken from al-aʿḍāʾ (limbs).
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is a good view, i.e. they divided up what they said. And he recited:
* "وَلَيْسَ دِينُ اللَّهِ بالمُعَضَّى" *
(And the religion of Allah is not one to be cut into pieces.)
i.e. not divided.
Al-Farrāʾ held that it is taken from al-ʿiḍāh, which are (thorny) trees.
And al-Kisāʾī held that it may be taken from both.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينََ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, recite the Qurʾān aloud in the prayer.
He said: And from it: تَصَدَّع القومُ, when the people disperse.
He said: And from it al-ṣudāʿ (headache), because it is a splitting of the sutures of the head.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known among the people of language that one says صَدَع بالحق when he makes it clear and manifest; it is as if (it says): make clear and make manifest.
Abū ʿUbayda recited (the verse) of Abū Dhuʾayb describing a herd of wild asses and jennies, and that he (the stallion) rules over them:
وكَأَنَّهُنَّ رِبابةٌ وكأَنَّه * يَسَرٌ يُفِيضُ على القِدَاحِ ويَصْدَعُ
(As if they were a bundle of gaming arrows, and he a gambler who shuffles the arrows and declares (the winning one).)
And from this the dawn is called ṣadīʿ, as he said:
* "كأنَّ بَيَاضَ لَبَّتِه صَدِيعُ" *
(As if the whiteness of its breast were the breaking dawn.)
And Abū l-ʿAbbās (al-Mubarrad) held that the meaning is: split falsehood with what you are commanded, i.e. separate (it).

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاكَ ٱلْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ﴾.
"Abū Bakr" Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda — and ʿUthmān al-Jazarī from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās — regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاكَ ٱلْمُسْتَهْزِئِينَ﴾. [Translator's note: so printed; the chain is presumably "Salama ibn Shabīb, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq".] They both said: "The mockers" were al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, ʿAdī ibn Qays, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth and al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib. They passed one by one by the Prophet ﷺ while Jibrīl, peace be upon him, was with him; and whenever one of them passed, Jibrīl said to him: How do you find this one? He would say: An evil servant of Allah. And Jibrīl would say: We have sufficed you against him.
As for al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, he stumbled, and an arrow caught in his cloak; he went to sit down and it cut his median vein (akḥal), and he bled until he died.
As for al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, a branch with thorns was brought, and his face was struck with it, so that his eyeballs ran down over his face. He used to say: I made a prayer against Muḥammad and he made a prayer against me, and mine was answered and his was answered. He prayed against me that I be blind, and I became blind; and I prayed against him that he be alone and outcast among the people of Yathrib, and so he was.
As for al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, he trod on a thorn, and his flesh fell away from his bones until he perished.
As for al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib and ʿAdī ibn Qays, one of them got up in the night, at ease, to drink from a jar, and he kept drinking until his belly burst and he died; and as for the other, a snake bit him and he died.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَكُنْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّاجِدِينََ﴾.
That is, be among those who pray.

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: Except three verses, which were revealed between Mecca and Medina when the Prophet ﷺ returned from Uḥud — Ḥamza having been killed and mutilated. The Prophet said: "I will surely mutilate thirty of them," and the Muslims said: "We will surely mutilate them." So Allah sent down ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُم فعَاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقبْتُم بِهِ﴾ to the end of three verses.
[Translator's note: this passage is filed under 15:99 but evidently belongs to the introduction of Sūrat al-Naḥl (16), whose Meccan revelation is being stated, with the exception of three verses (16:126–128).]

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab
(الر) disconnected letters, with no grammatical position. (تلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the overt sukūn on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; and (اللام) indicates distance, and (الكاف) indicates address. (آيات) khabar, nominative. (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (قرآن) conjoined to الكتاب by the wāw, genitive. (مبين) naʿt of القرآن, genitive.
The nominal sentence has no grammatical position; it is an initial sentence (ibtidāʾiyya).

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab
(ربما) kāffa and makfūfa. (يودّ) an imperfect verb, nominative. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil. (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative, fāʿil. (لو) a maṣdar particle. (كانوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, and (الواو) is in the position of a nominative, the ism (subject) of kāna. (مسلمين) khabar of كانوا, accusative, its accusative marking being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (لو كانوا مسلمين) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi, the governing word being يودّ.
The clause «يودّ الذين ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الّذين).
The clause «كانوا مسلمين» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (لو).

* Rhetoric:
1- Expression by the opposite: in His saying, the Exalted, رُبَما يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ كانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ, the scholars of rhetoric differed over what is meant by this expression. The grammarians have established that ربما enters only upon the past tense? And what is meant by the sense of "fewness" that رب conveys? The first question was answered by saying that what is anticipated in the reports of Allah the Exalted is in the position of the past whose realisation is certain, as if it had been said: "often they wished". The second was answered by saying that this is a way that occurs in the usage of the Arabs, as in their saying "perhaps you will regret your deed", and "often a person regrets what he does", where they have no doubt about his regret and do not intend to make it few. Sensible people guard against exposing themselves to the merely conjectured just as they guard against the established certainty. This answer is beautiful, but more beautiful than it is to say: the Arabs express a meaning by what conveys the opposite of what they intend.

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab
(ذرهم) an imperative verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (هم) is an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, obligatorily so, its implied form being "you". (يأكلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis of a request, its jussive marking being the dropping of the nūn; and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (الواو) conjunction. (يتمتّعوا) like يأكلوا, and conjoined to it. (الواو) conjunction. (يلههم) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to يأكلوا, its jussive marking being the dropping of the weak letter; and (هم) is like the first. (الأمل) fāʿil, nominative. (الفاء) the linking particle of the apodosis of an implied condition. (سوف) a particle of futurity. (يعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the retention of the nūn; and (الواو) is the fāʿil, while the object of يعلمون is omitted, its implied form being "the outcome of their affair".
The clause «ذرهم ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يأكلوا ....» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined by the fāʾ.
That is: "if you leave them, they will eat ..".
The clause «يتمتّعوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يأكلوا.
The clause «يلههم الأمل ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يأكلوا.
The clause «سوف يعلمون» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if the affair of this world occupies them, then they will know".

* Morphology:
(الأمل): a samāʿī maṣdar (a verbal noun taken by hearing) of the verb أمل; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (ما) negative. (أهلكنا) a past verb together with its fāʿil. (من) a redundant preposition, for the inclusion of the whole genus. (قرية) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi. (إلّا) for restriction. (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl. (اللام) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to a fronted khabar. (كتاب) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (معلوم) naʿt of كتاب, nominative.
The clause «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «لها كتاب ...» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from قرية because of the presence of the wāw.

* Morphology:
(معلوم): a passive participle of the triliteral علم; its wazn is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab
(ما) a particle of negation. (تسبق) an imperfect verb, nominative. (من) a redundant preposition, for the inclusion of the whole genus. (أمّة) genitive in form, nominative in position, fāʿil of تسبق. (أجلها) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (ها) is a pronoun in genitive construct. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) like the first. (يستأخرون) an imperfect verb, nominative; and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
The clause «ما تسبق ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «ما يستأخرون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ما تسبق.

safi-cedvel:6-7.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (قالوا) a past verb together with its fāʿil. (يا) a vocative particle. (أيّ) the one addressed, a specific indefinite, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative; and (ها) is a particle of alerting. (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, ʿaṭf bayān of أيّ, or a badal. (نزّل) a passive past verb. (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (نزّل). (الذكر) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. (إنّك) a particle resembling the verb, a naskh (abrogating) particle, and (الكاف) is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the ism of إنّ. (اللام) the shifted lām, for emphasis. (مجنون) khabar of إنّ, nominative.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its answer» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نزّل عليه الذكر ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «إنّك لمجنون» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the vocative.
(لوما) a particle of offering. (تأتينا) an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ; and (نا) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, while the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". (بالملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأتينا). (إن) a particle of jussive condition. (كنت) a defective past verb, a naskh verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis. And (التاء) is a pronoun in the position of a nominative, the ism of كان. (من الصادقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of كنت, its genitive marking being the yāʾ.
The clause «تأتينا ...» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «كنت من الصادقين» has no grammatical position; resumptive. And the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is: "if you are one of the truthful in what you claim, then bring us the angels".

* Morphology:
(مجنون): a passive participle of the triliteral جنّ; its wazn is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:10-11.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of affirmation. (أرسلنا) like نزّلنا [[in the preceding verse (9).]]. (من قبلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أرسلنا), and (الكاف) is a pronoun in genitive construct. (في شيع) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of the implied object, that is: "We sent messengers among the sects". (الأوّلين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marking being the yāʾ [[and it is originally an adjective of an omitted described noun, that is: "the sects of the earlier nations".]].
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to an implied oath.
(الواو) conjunction. (ما) a particle of negation. (يأتيهم) an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ; and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (من) a redundant preposition. (رسول) genitive in form, nominative in position, fāʿil of يأتي. (إلّا) for restriction. (كانوا) a defective past verb, and (الواو) is the ism of كان. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يستهزئون), which is an imperfect verb, nominative; and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
The clause «ما يأتيهم من رسول ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أرسلنا [[or to the implied oath clause.]].
The clause «كانوا.. يستهزئون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the object of يأتيهم.
The clause «يستهزئون» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كانوا. [[Or from رسول; but it is not valid as an adjective of رسول.]]

* Morphology:
(شيع): plural of شيعة, a noun for a group agreed upon a path. In al-Miṣbāḥ: every people who gathered upon a matter are a shiʿa. It then became a name for a particular group. The wazn of شيعة is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn, and the wazn of شيع is فعل, with kasra then fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
Scrambled laff and nashr in His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ. Then He followed that with His saying وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ to the end of the verse, meaning that this is their habit, and the habit of the Jāhiliyya with all the prophets; so do not grieve, but follow those before you and take them as your example.
It is applied to:
[Translator's note: the source text breaks off here with the incomplete phrase «يطلق على:» and nothing follows it in the entry.]

safi-cedvel:12-13.t:
* I'rab
(الكاف) a preposition of comparison. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governing word is نسلك; the reference is to the mockery and the denial. (اللام) indicates distance and (الكاف) indicates address. (نسلكه) an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is "We", for magnification, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi [[the commentators differed over the referent of the pronoun. Al-Zamakhsharī said that it refers to الذكر, and the reference of the demonstrative, for him, is to the "threading" (salk). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said that it refers to the mockery and the polytheism. It is related from Mujāhid: "We thread the denial". Abū Ḥayyān prefers Ibn ʿAṭiyya's view ...]]. (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نسلكه). (المجرمين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marking being the yāʾ.
The clause «نسلكه ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(لا) negative. (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative; and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يؤمنون); the bāʾ is causal, and the pronoun refers to the demonstrative [[it is permissible for (به) to be attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil of the negated يؤمنون, that is: "mocking it".]]. (الواو) resumptive. (قد) a particle of affirmation. (خلت) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, and (التاء) is for the feminine. (سنّة) fāʿil, nominative. (الأولين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marking being the yāʾ.
The clause «لا يؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), or an explanation of (نسلكه) [[or in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the pronoun in نسلكه, that is: "not believed in" (passive participle form), the third-person pronoun being الذكر.]].
The clause «خلت سنّة الأولين» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
- Analogical simile (tashbīh tamthīlī): in His saying, the Exalted, كَذلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ etc....
The speech contains an analogical simile for the obstinacy that has taken hold of them, the obstinacy firmly rooted in their breasts. The detail of it is that Allah the Exalted threaded the Qur'an into their hearts and made it enter their innermost cores, just as He threaded it into the hearts of the believers who affirm its truth; so these denied it and those affirmed it, each upon knowledge and clear proof, so that whoever perishes may perish upon clear proof and whoever lives may live upon clear proof, and so that the disbelievers may have no argument against Allah that they did not understand the aspects of the inimitability as those who believed understood them. So Allah the Exalted informed them from now, while they are still in a respite and possibility, that they disbelieved only with knowledge, being obstinate and transgressing, so that it may be more refuting of any argument they fabricate and more negating of every claim they make.

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (فتحنا) a past verb together with its fāʿil. (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (فتحنا). (بابا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of (بابا). (الفاء) conjunction. (ظلّوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, and (الواو) is the ism of ظلّ. (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يعرجون), which is an imperfect verb, nominative; and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
The clause «فتحنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «ظلّوا.. يعرجون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يعرجون» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of ظلّوا.
(اللام) occurring in the answer to لو. (قالوا) a past verb together with its fāʿil. (إنّما) kāffa and makfūfa. (سكّرت) a passive past verb; and (التاء) is for the feminine. (أبصارنا) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; and (نا) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (بل) for transitional iḍrāb (turning away). (نحن) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ. (قوم) khabar, nominative. (مسحورون) naʿt of قوم, nominative, its nominative marking being the wāw.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the non-jussive condition (لو).
The clause «سكّرت أبصارنا ...» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «نحن قوم ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مسحورون): plural of مسحور, a passive participle of the triliteral سحر; its wazn is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّما سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصارُنا, they meant by it that our sight has been corrupted and a defect has befallen its perception, just as that befalls the mind of the drunkard so that his perception is impaired.
2- In the two words of restriction and iḍrāb there is an indication that they build their saying upon this, and that what they see has no reality, but is a matter made to appear to them through sorcery. The clarification of this is that they said "إنما", which conveys restriction to what is mentioned last, so the restriction falls on the eyes and not on the "intoxication"; as if they said: our eyes were intoxicated, not our minds. And though we imagine these things with our eyes, we know with our minds that the situation is otherwise, that is, that it has no reality. Then they said "بل", as if they turned away from restricting it to the eyes and said: rather it went beyond that to our minds through a sorcery he has wrought on us.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab
(ما) negative. (ننزّل) an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is "We", for magnification. (الملائكة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (إلّا) for restriction. (بالحق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from الملائكة [[or attached to (ننزّل), the bāʾ being for aid (istiʿāna). Al-Zamakhsharī made it an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is: "except a sending-down accompanied by the truth".]]. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) like the first. (كانوا) a defective past verb, and (الواو) is the ism of كان. (إذا) a particle of response with no governing effect. (منظرين) khabar of كانوا, accusative, its accusative marking being the yāʾ.
The clause «ما ننزّل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «ما كانوا.. منظرين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
- Scrambled laff and nashr (enumeration followed by distribution): in His saying, the Exalted, ما نُنَزِّلُ الْمَلائِكَةَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَما كانُوا إِذاً مُنْظَرِينَ.
The speech is directed by Him, Glorified, to His Prophet ﷺ, as an answer to their reported saying and a rejection of their false proposal, which arose from sheer partisanship and obstinacy, namely their saying لَوْ ما تَأْتِينا بِالْمَلائِكَةِ. As for His reply to their first saying, namely إِنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ, it is His saying, the Exalted, which comes next: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab
(إنّ) a particle of emphasis that governs the accusative, and (نا) is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the ism of إنّ. (نحن) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ [[or a pronoun borrowed for the position of the accusative, as tawkīd of the ism of إنّ.]]. (نزّلنا) a past verb together with its fāʿil. (الذكر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (إنّا) like the first. (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (حافظون). (اللام) the shifted lām, for emphasis. (حافظون) khabar of إنّ, nominative, its nominative marking being the wāw.
The clause «إنّا نحن نزّلنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «نحن نزّلنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «نزّلنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ نحن.
The clause «إنّا له لحافظون» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:16-20.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of affirmation. (جعلنا) a past verb together with its fāʿil. (في السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جعلنا) in the sense of "We created" [[if it is transitive to two objects, the prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted element which is the second object.]]. (بروجا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (زيّناها) like جعلنا, and (ها) is mafʿūl bihi. (للناظرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun [[or attached to (زيّناها), the lām being the lām of semantic ownership.]].
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.
The clause «زيّناها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جعلنا.
(الواو) conjunction. (حفظناها من كلّ) like زيّناها للناظرين, and the prepositional phrase is attached to (حفظناها). (شيطان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (رجيم) naʿt of شيطان, genitive.
The clause «حفظناها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جعلناها.
(إلّا) a particle of exception. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as a discontinuous or continuous exception [[that is: "but whoever eavesdrops, the meteor snatches him", or "whoever eavesdrops hears something of their news". Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī allowed (من) to be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause أتبعه, with the fāʾ redundant because of the mubtadaʾ's resemblance to a condition; the exception is then discontinuous.]]. (استرق) a past verb; the fāʿil is "he", which is the returning pronoun. (السمع) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الفاء) conjunction. (أتبعه) like استرق, and (الهاء) is mafʿūl bihi. (شهاب) fāʿil, nominative. (مبين) naʿt of شهاب, nominative.
The clause «استرق ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «أتبعه شهاب ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(الواو) conjunction. (الأرض) mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb in the manner of ishtighāl (preoccupation), explained by what comes after it. (مددناها) like زيّناها. (الواو) conjunction. (ألقينا) like جعلنا. (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ألقينا). (رواسي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (وأنبتنا فيها) like وألقينا فيها. (من كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of an implied element, that is: "kinds of every thing". (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (موزون) naʿt of شيء, genitive.
The clause «(مددنا) الأرض ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جعلنا ...
The clause «مددناها (the mentioned one)» has no grammatical position; explicative.
The clause «ألقينا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (مددنا) الأرض.
The clause «أنبتنا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (مددنا) الأرض.
(الواو) conjunction. (جعلنا) like the first. (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (جعلنا) in the sense of "We created" [[if it is transitive to two objects, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element which is the second object]]. (فيها) like the preceding, attached to (جعلنا). (معايش) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) conjunction. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, conjoined to معايش [[and it is, in the opinion of al-Zajjāj, mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "We provided livelihood for those whom you are not ..."; and it is said that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, as the meaning indicates it, that is: "those whom you are not providers for, We made livelihoods for them in it". The Kufans, and with them al-Akhfash, said it is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the pronoun in (لكم).]]. (لستم) a defective, inert past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (تم) is a pronoun, the ism of ليس. (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) in the position of a genitive, attached to رازقين. (الباء) a redundant preposition. (رازقين) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar of ليس, its genitive marking being the yāʾ.
The clause «جعلنا لكم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause (مددنا) الأرض.
The clause «لستم.. برازقين» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(شهاب): an inert noun for a burning body that falls from the sky; its wazn is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ; its plural is شهب, with two ḍammas.
(موزون): a passive participle of the triliteral وزن; its wazn is مفعول.
(معايش): plural of معيشة, a noun for that by which a person lives during his lifetime of food, drink, and clothing. The wazn of معيشة is مفعلة, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, and it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by sukūn, in that the yāʾ was given sukūn and its vowel was moved to the ʿayn before it. The yāʾ was not turned into a hamza in (معايش) because it is original.

* Rhetoric:
- Figurative usage (majāz): in His saying, the Exalted, مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْزُونٍ, that is: measured by a specific measure that wisdom requires. It is a majāz used for a necessary concomitant of its meaning, or a kināya; or it means "of everything pleasing and well proportioned", from their saying: "a well-measured (balanced) speech".

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (إن) negative. (من) a redundant preposition. (شيء) genitive in form, nominative in position, mubtadaʾ. (إلّا) for restriction. (عندنا) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (نا) is a pronoun in genitive construct. (خزائنه) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative.
And (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative. (ننزّله) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الهاء) is mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is "We", for magnification. (إلّا) like the first. (بقدر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ننزّله) [[or attached to an omitted ḥāl from the object, that is: "accompanied by a known measure".]]. (معلوم) naʿt of قدر, genitive.
The clause «إن من شيء إلّا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «عندنا خزائنه ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (شيء).
The clause «ننزّله ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(قدر): a noun for what Allah decrees, and for the attachment of the will to its times; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
- Metaphor: in His saying, the Exalted, وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا عِنْدَنا خَزائِنُهُ. His unseen, countless decreed things, which fall under His all-encompassing power, are likened, in being concealed from the knowledge of all the worlds and guarded from their hands reaching them, to the precious goods stored in royal treasuries. So the mention of "treasuries" is in the manner of imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra takhyīliyya). It is also allowed that His power over everything, and His bringing into being whatever He wills, is likened to treasuries in which things are deposited, prepared so that He may bring out of them what He wills; so this is mentioned by way of analogical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya).

* Benefits:
وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ.
This «إن» is negative, and that is why «من» comes after it, which is a redundant preposition that occurs to give emphasis. «إن» has several kinds. We have treated them fully elsewhere earlier, so we content ourselves with merely recalling them here.

safi-cedvel:22-25.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (أرسلنا) a past verb together with its fāʿil. (الرياح) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (لواقح) ḥāl, accusative. (الفاء) conjunction. (أنزلنا ... ماء) like أرسلنا الرياح. (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزلنا). (الفاء) conjunction. (أسقينا) like أرسلنا, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and (الميم) is for the masculine plural, and (الواو) is redundant, the filling out of the vowel of the mīm, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, a second mafʿūl bihi. (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl. (ما) negative, working like ليس. (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, its ism. (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to خازنين. (الباء) a redundant preposition. (خازنين) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar of ما.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أنزلنا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أرسلنا.
The clause «أسقيناكموه ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أنزلنا.
The clause «ما أنتم ... بخازنين» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the second-person pronoun in (أسقيناكم) [[that is: "while you are unable to bring it into being".]].
(الواو) conjunction. (إنّا) a particle of emphasis that governs the accusative, and (نا) is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the ism of إن. (اللام) the shifted lām, for emphasis. (نحن) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the clause نحيي. (نحيي) an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ; the fāʿil is "We", for magnification. (الواو) conjunction. (نميت) an imperfect verb, nominative. (نحن) like the first. (الوارثون) the second khabar of نحن, nominative, its nominative marking being the wāw.
The clause «إنّا لنحن ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أسقيناكموه.
The clause «نحن نحيي ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «نحيي ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of نحن.
The clause «نميت ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause نحيي.
The clause «نحن الوارثون» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause نحن نحيي.
(الواو) conjunction. (اللام) the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of affirmation. (علمنا) like أرسلنا. (المستقدمين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its accusative marking being the yāʾ. (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun, in the position of a genitive, attached to a ḥāl from المستقدمين. (ولقد علمنا المستأخرين) like the preceding one.
The clause «قد علمنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause إنّا لنحن..
The clause «قد علمنا (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause is conjoined to the first oath clause.
(الواو) conjunction. (إنّ) like the first. (ربك) the ism of إنّ, accusative, and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi. (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ. (يحشرهم) like نميت, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "He". (إنّه) like إنّا. (حكيم) khabar of إنّ, nominative. (عليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إنّ ربّك هو ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the implied oath clause.
The clause «هو يحشرهم ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يحشرهم ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of هو.
The clause «إنّه حكيم ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(لواقح): plural of لاقحة, feminine of لاقح, an active participle of the triliteral لقح [[it is said that it is the plural of ملقح (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the qāf) from the quadriliteral ألقح, whose plural is ملاقح, and then the mīm was dropped for lightness. In al-Mukhtār: "the stallion impregnated (alqaḥa) the she-camel, and the wind the clouds; and 'impregnating winds' is ريح لواقح, and do not say ملاقح, for it is among the rarities", end. And in al-Muḥīṭ: "the winds impregnated (alqaḥat) the trees, so they are لواقح and ملاقح".]]; its wazn is فاعل.
(خازنين): plural of خازن, an active participle of the triliteral خزن; its wazn is فاعل.
(المستقدمين): plural of المستقدم, an active participle of the sextiliteral استقدم; its wazn is مستفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(المستأخرين): plural of المستأخر, an active participle of the sextiliteral استأخر; its wazn is مستفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
- Eloquent simile (tashbīh baligh): in His saying, the Exalted, وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّياحَ لَواقِحَ. اللواقح is the plural of لاقح, meaning "pregnant", and the winds are described thus by way of the eloquent simile: the wind laden with rain-bearing cloud is likened to a pregnant she-camel, because it carries that cloud or the water in it. What is meant is "impregnators" of the cloud or the trees, so that "impregnation" (laqḥ) is borrowed for the pouring of rain into the cloud or the trees.

safi-cedvel:26-27.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (لقد خلقنا الإنسان) like لقد علمنا المستقدمين [[in verse (24) of this sura.]]. (من صلصال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خلقنا). (من حمأ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of صلصال [[or it is a badal from صلصال with the repetition of the preposition.]]. (مسنون) naʿt of حمأ, genitive.
The clause «خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to an implied oath.. and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(الواو) conjunction. (الجانّ خلقناه) like الأرض [[in verse (19) of this sura]] مددناها. (من) a preposition. (قبل) a noun indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of a genitive, attached to (خلقناه). (من نار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خلقناه). (السموم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «(خلقنا) الجانّ ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause خلقنا الإنسان.
The clause «خلقناه ...» has no grammatical position; explicative.

* Morphology:
(صلصال): a noun for dry clay; its wazn is فعلال.
(حمأ): a noun for black mud; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(مسنون): a passive participle of the triliteral سنّ; its wazn is مفعول.
(الجانّ): a collective noun for the jinn, and it is on the wazn فاعل; its plural is جنّان, with kasra on the jīm and a doubled fatḥa on the nūn.
(السموم): a noun for the hot wind, or the fire that has no smoke; its wazn is فعول, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:28-29.t:
* I'rab
(الواو) resumptive. (إذ) an adverbial noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember". (قال) a past verb. (ربّك) fāʿil, nominative, and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi. (للملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قال). (إنّي) like إنّا [[in verse (23) of this sura.]]. (خالق) khabar of إنّ, nominative. (بشرا) mafʿūl bihi of the active participle خالق, accusative. (من صلصال من حمأ مسنون) their i'rab has already been given [[in verse (26) of this sura]], and the first genitive phrase is attached to خالق.
The clause «قال ربك ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إنّي خالق ...» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
(الفاء) conjunction. (إذا) an adverb of future time, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, attached to the content of the answer. (سوّيت) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (التاء) is the fāʿil and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الواو) conjunction. (نفخت) like سوّيت. (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (نفخت). (من روحي) a preposition attached to نفخت, its genitive marking being the implied kasra on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) the linking particle of the apodosis. (قعوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the nūn ...
and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (له) [Translator's note: the source reads «(له) فيه متعلّق ب (قعوا)», where فيه appears to be a slip for the intended wording; translated as written: "(له) in it attached to (قعوا)"] [[or attached to ساجدين..]]. (ساجدين) ḥāl, accusative, its accusative marking being the yāʾ.
The clause «سوّيته ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نفخت ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause سوّيته.
The clause «قعوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to a non-jussive condition.

safi-cedvel:30-31.t:
* I'rab
(الفاء) resumptive. (سجد) a past verb. (الملائكة) fāʿil, nominative. (كلّهم) tawkīd maʿnawī (semantic emphasis) of الملائكة, nominative like it, and (هم) is an attached pronoun in genitive construct. (أجمعون) a second semantic tawkīd, nominative, its nominative marking being the wāw.
The clause «سجد الملائكة ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(إلّا) a particle of exception. (إبليس) a noun, accusative as a discontinuous or continuous exception, according to the well-known disagreement over the reality of Iblīs, whether he is of the angels or not. (أبى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif; the fāʿil is "he". (أن) a particle of accusative and of maṣdar. (يكون) a defective imperfect verb, accusative, its ism a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he". (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted khabar of يكون. (الساجدين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marking being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكون ...) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi, the governing word being أبى «1».
The clause «أبى ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab
(قال) a past verb; the fāʿil is "He". (يا) a vocative particle. (إبليس) the one addressed, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, a singular proper name. (ما) an interrogative noun, for rebuke, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ. (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to the khabar of ما. (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative. (لا) negative. (تكون مع الساجدين) like يكون مع الساجدين «2», and its ism is "you". The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تكون ...) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, namely في, attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is: "What is with you in your not being with the prostrators", that is: what is your excuse, while you are not prostrating with the others.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يا إبليس مالك ...» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying. [[In the preceding verse (31).]] And the clause «مالك ...» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the vocative.

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab
(قال) like the preceding [[in the preceding verse (32).]]. (لم) a particle of negation and jussive. (أكن) a defective imperfect verb, jussive, its ism a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I". (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd). (أسجد) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of denial; the fāʿil is "I". (لبشر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسجد).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أسجد ...) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted khabar of أكن.
(خلقته) like سوّيته [[in verse (29) of this sura.
(3, 4) in verse (26) of this sura.]]. (من صلصال ... مسنون) their i'rab has already been given «3».
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لم أكن ...» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «أسجد ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «خلقته ...» is in the position of a genitive, naʿt of بشر.

safi-cedvel:34-35.t:
* I'rab
(قال) like the preceding «4». (الفاء) the linking particle of the apodosis of an implied condition. (اخرج) an imperative verb; the fāʿil is "you". (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (اخرج). (الفاء) causal. (إنّك) a particle of emphasis that governs the accusative, and (الكاف) is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the ism of إنّ. (رجيم) khabar of إنّ, nominative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «اخرج ...» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you are not content with prostration, then go out".. and the implied conditional clause is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «إنّك رجيم» has no grammatical position; causal.
(الواو) conjunction. (إنّ) like the first. (على) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to the fronted khabar of إنّ. (اللعنة) the postponed ism of إنّ, accusative. (إلى يوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to اللعنة [[or attached to the "settledness" (istiqrār) which is the khabar.]]. (الدين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «إنّ عليك اللعنة ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause إنّك رجيم.

* Rhetoric:
- Kināya (indirect expression): in His saying, the Exalted, فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ, that is: driven away from all good and honour, for one who is driven away is stoned with stones; so the speech is of the type of kināya.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab
(قال) a past verb; the fāʿil is "he", Iblīs. (ربّ) the one addressed, a muḍāf from which the vocative particle is omitted, accusative, its accusative marking being the implied fatḥa on what precedes the yāʾ that was dropped for lightness.. and the omitted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) the linking particle of the apodosis of an implied condition. (انظرني) an imperative verb of supplication, and (النون) is protective and (الياء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, while the fāʿil is "you". (إلى يوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنظر). (يبعثون) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the retention of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption.
The clause «the vocative and its answer» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «انظرني ...» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if You drove me away and cursed me, then grant me respite".. and the implied conditional clause has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the vocative.
The clause «يبعثون» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.

safi-cedvel:37-38.t:
* I'rab
(قال) like the preceding [[in verse (36).]]. (الفاء) the linking particle of the apodosis of an implied condition. (إنّك) its i'rab has already been given [[in verse (34) of this sura.]]. (من المنظرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of إنّ, its genitive marking being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
